docs.title: Documentation Template Guide
docs.text: This guide provides a template for documenting additional sections in the theme. Use this as a reference when creating documentation for the remaining 40+ sections.

docs.title: Standard Section Documentation Structure
docs.text: Every section documentation file should follow this structure:

docs.title: 1. Title and Introduction (Required)
docs.text:
# [Section Name]

[2-3 sentences describing what the section does and its purpose]

Use this section to:
- [Benefit/use case 1]
- [Benefit/use case 2]
- [Benefit/use case 3]
- [Benefit/use case 4]

docs.title: 2. Adding and Managing (Required)
docs.text:
Always include this exact text:

---

## Adding and Managing This Section

This [is a flexible/versatile] section that can be added to [most pages/any page/specific pages] in your store. To learn how to add, remove, or reorder sections on your page, please refer to Shopify's official guide on [Using sections and blocks](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-store/themes/theme-structure/sections-and-blocks).

---

docs.title: 3. Section Settings (Required)
docs.text:
Document ALL settings from the schema:

## Section Settings

### [Setting Group Name]

* **[Setting Label]** — [User-friendly description of what this does and how to use it]. [Additional context if needed]. Default: [default value].

Guidelines for writing setting descriptions: - Use "Choose," "Control," "Set," "Select" to start action-oriented descriptions - Always mention the range for numeric settings (e.g., "Range: 10-50px") - Always mention the default value - If a setting only appears conditionally, note it: "(Only visible when [condition])" - Translate technical terms to user language: - ❌ "Padding top" → ✅ "Space inside the top of the section" - ❌ "Color scheme" → ✅ "Color scheme — Choose the colors for this section's background and text"

docs.title: 4. Blocks (If Applicable)
docs.text:
If the section has blocks:

## Blocks

This section uses **[Block Type]** blocks. [Explanation of how blocks work in this section]

### [Block Type Name]

[Description of what this block does]

Settings:
* **[Setting 1]** — [Description]
* **[Setting 2]** — [Description]

If no blocks:

## Blocks

This section does not use blocks. [Alternative explanation, e.g., "Instead, products are selected directly in the **Product list** setting."]

docs.title: 5. Usage Tips (Recommended)
docs.text:
---

## Usage Tips

* **[Tip category]:** [Practical advice]
* **[Tip category]:** [Practical advice]
* **[Tip category]:** [Practical advice]

docs.title: 6. Footer (Required)
docs.text:
Always end with:

---

## Need Help?

For more information about working with sections in Shopify themes, visit [Shopify's Help Center](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-store/themes/theme-structure/sections-and-blocks).

docs.title: Translation Key Reference
docs.text:
When you see t: keys in the schema, refer to these translation files: - /locales/en.default.schema.json — Contains all English translations - /locales/nl.schema.json — Dutch translations (for reference)

Common translation paths: - t:generic.common.* — Common settings used across sections - t:sections.section_[name].settings.* — Section-specific settings - t:sections.section_[name].blocks.* — Block-specific settings

docs.title: Standard Spacing Controls
docs.text:
When you see these in a schema:

{
  "type": "select",
  "id": "mt",
  "label": "t:generic.common.mt"
}

Document as:

Margin top — Control the top margin (space above the section). Choose between Standard or None.

docs.title: Color Scheme Setting
docs.text:
{
  "type": "color_scheme",
  "id": "color_scheme",
  "label": "t:generic.common.color_scheme"
}

Document as:

Color scheme — Choose the color scheme for this section's background and text. Default: [check default value].

docs.title: Range Settings
docs.text:
{
  "type": "range",
  "id": "setting_name",
  "min": 0,
  "max": 100,
  "step": 5,
  "unit": "px",
  "default": 50
}

Document as:

[Label] — [Description of what it controls]. Range: [min]-[max][unit]. Default: [default][unit].

docs.title: Conditional Visibility
docs.text:
{
  "type": "text",
  "id": "button_label",
  "visible_if": "{{ section.settings.show_button }}"
}

Document as:

[Label] — [Description]. (Only visible when [condition])

docs.title: Tone
docs.text:
• Friendly and encouraging — Write like you're helping a friend
  • Clear and simple — No jargon or technical terms
  • Patient — Assume the reader is new to Shopify
  • Action-oriented — Tell them what they CAN do, not what the setting IS

docs.title: Formatting
docs.text:
• Use bold for setting names (exactly as they appear in the Theme Editor)
  • Use code formatting for technical terms, filenames, or values
  • Use bullet points for lists of settings
  • Use numbered lists only for step-by-step instructions

docs.title: Language
docs.text:
• ✅ "Choose the color for..." (active voice)
  • ❌ "The color can be chosen..." (passive voice)
  • ✅ "This creates a more spacious look" (benefit-focused)
  • ❌ "This adds 20px of padding" (technical)
  • ✅ "Range: 10-50px. Default: 30px." (clear format)
  • ❌ "Accepts values from 10 to 50" (wordy)

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
To continue documenting sections:

  1. Choose a section from the priority list
  2. Read the section file in /sections/[section-name].liquid
  3. Find the schema (look for {% schema %})
  4. Check translations in /locales/en.default.schema.json
  5. Follow the template in this guide
  6. Save the file as /docs/en/section-[name].md
  7. Update the README.md to include a link to the new documentation

docs.title: Questions to Answer in Each Documentation
docs.text:

Good luck documenting! Remember: every setting you document helps a store owner customize their site with confidence! 🎉

docs.title: Articles Section
docs.text:
The Articles section displays blog posts from one of your blogs in a carousel slider. It's perfect for showcasing recent articles, featured posts, or blog content on your homepage or other pages.

This section helps drive traffic to your blog and keeps customers engaged with your content.

docs.title: Adding or Managing the Section
docs.text:
1. From your Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Themes
  2. Click Customize on your current theme
  3. Navigate to the page where you want articles to appear (typically your homepage)
  4. Click Add section and select Articles
  5. Configure settings and select which blog to display

docs.title: Colors & Layout
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the background color and text style for the section. Default: Scheme 2.
  • Alignment — Position content left, center, or right. Default: Center.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
• Section type — Control the section width:
  • Container — Content stays within standard page width
  • Full width — Content stretches edge-to-edge

Default: Full width.

  • Section height — Background height behavior:
  • Auto — Background adjusts to content
  • Fixed — Background has a set height percentage

Default: Auto.

  • Section background height — If using Fixed height, set the background size. Range: 0-100%. Default: 80%. (Only visible when Section height is "Fixed")

docs.title: Blog Selection
docs.text:
• Blog — Select which blog to display articles from. You must create blogs in your Shopify admin first (Online Store > Blog Posts).

Note: The section automatically displays articles from the selected blog in reverse chronological order (newest first).

docs.title: Carousel Settings
docs.text:
• Slides per view (desktop) — How many articles show at once on desktop. Range: 2-6 articles. Default: 3.
  • Slides per view (tablet) — How many articles show on tablets. Options: 1-4.5 slides or Automatic. Default: 2.
  • Slides per view (phone) — How many articles show on mobile. Options: 1-4 slides or Automatic. Default: 1.
  • Carousel overflow — Enable to show a peek of the next article, encouraging scrolling. Default: Disabled.
  • Slider pagination — Show dot indicators below the carousel for navigation. Default: Enabled.
  • Alternate offset — Stagger every other article slightly lower for visual interest. Default: Disabled.

docs.title: Spacing
docs.text:
• Margin top — Space above the section. Options: Standard or None. Default: Standard.
  • Margin bottom — Space below the section. Options: Standard or None. Default: Standard.
  • Padding top — Inner spacing at the top. Options: Standard or None. Default: Standard.
  • Padding bottom — Inner spacing at the bottom. Options: Standard or None. Default: Standard.

docs.title: Content Settings
docs.text:
The section includes standard content blocks you can add:

  • Heading — Section title (e.g., "From Our Blog" or "Latest Articles")
  • Subheading — Additional descriptive text
  • Text — Paragraph content introducing your blog
  • Button — Call-to-action button (e.g., "Read More" linking to your full blog)

See the Content Section documentation for details on using these content blocks.

docs.title: Article Cards
docs.text:
Each article in the carousel displays: - Featured image - Article title - Excerpt (if available) - Publication date - Author (if enabled in theme settings) - "Read more" link

The appearance of article cards is controlled by your theme's global card settings (Theme Settings > Cards).

docs.title: Managing Blog Content
docs.text:
Articles are created and managed in your Shopify admin:

  1. Go to Online Store > Blog Posts
  2. Select the blog you want to add to
  3. Click Add blog post
  4. Enter the title, content, and featured image
  5. Publish your article

The Articles section automatically displays published posts from your selected blog.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Homepage placement: The Articles section works great on your homepage to showcase content and establish authority.

  • Blog selection: If you have multiple blogs (like "News" and "Guides"), you can add multiple Articles sections to different pages, each displaying a different blog.

  • Featured images: Always add eye-catching featured images to your blog posts. They're prominently displayed in the article cards.

  • Excerpt quality: Write compelling excerpts that entice readers to click through. Shopify automatically creates excerpts if you don't provide one, but custom excerpts work better.

  • Number of articles: Show 3-4 articles on desktop for the best visual balance. Too many makes cards too small.

  • Regular updates: Keep your blog active. An outdated "Latest Articles" section with old dates can make your store seem inactive.

  • Call-to-action: Add a "View All Articles" button that links to your full blog page, encouraging deeper exploration.

  • Content strategy: Use your blog for:

  • Product guides and how-tos
  • Industry news and trends
  • Customer stories and testimonials
  • Behind-the-scenes content
  • SEO-optimized content for relevant keywords

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Consistent publishing: Maintain a regular posting schedule so there's always fresh content in this section.

  • Visual consistency: Use similar image styles and dimensions for all blog featured images (recommended: 1200x800px or 16:9 ratio).

  • Compelling titles: Write clear, benefit-driven article titles that make people want to click.

  • Mobile optimization: Test how article cards look on mobile devices. Ensure images and text remain readable.

  • Link to blog: Always provide a way for customers to access your complete blog, not just the carousel items.

  • SEO benefit: Blog content improves your store's SEO, driving organic traffic. Optimize articles with relevant keywords.

  • Engagement: Encourage comments and social sharing on your blog posts to increase engagement.

docs.title: Creating Blogs
docs.text:
If you haven't created a blog yet:

  1. Go to Online Store > Blog Posts in your Shopify admin
  2. Click Manage blogs
  3. Click Add blog
  4. Enter a title (like "News" or "Tips & Guides")
  5. Add SEO details if desired
  6. Save your blog
  7. Start adding blog posts

You can then select this blog in the Articles section settings.

docs.title: Common Section Titles
docs.text:
• "From Our Blog"
  • "Latest Articles"
  • "Recent Posts"
  • "Tips & Guides"
  • "What's New"
  • "Read Our Stories"
  • "Blog Highlights"

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about blogging on Shopify, visit: - Managing blogs and posts - Blog SEO best practices - Adding images to blog posts

docs.title: Image Banner Section
docs.text:
The Image Banner section creates a large, eye-catching hero banner with an image, heading, subheading, and optional buttons. This is perfect for making a strong first impression on your visitors or highlighting important announcements.

Use this section to: - Create a stunning homepage hero image - Announce sales, promotions, or new collections - Share your brand story with impactful visuals - Drive visitors to specific collections or products

docs.title: Adding and Managing This Section
docs.text: This versatile section can be added to any page in your store. To learn how to add, remove, or reorder sections on your page, please refer to Shopify's official guide on Using sections and blocks.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the color scheme for the text overlay and any background areas. Default: Scheme 2.
  • Section type — Choose the banner width:
  • Container — Banner stays within the content area with margins on the sides
  • Full width — Banner extends edge-to-edge across the screen

Default: Container. * Margin top — Control the top margin (space above the banner). Choose between Standard or None. * Margin bottom — Control the bottom margin (space below the banner). Choose between Standard or None.

docs.title: Image
docs.text:
• Image — Upload the main banner image. For best results, use a high-resolution image (at least 1800px wide).
  • Banner height — Set the height of your banner in pixels. Range: 300-800px. Default: 500px. Taller banners create more drama, while shorter banners leave more room for other content.
  • Overlay alignment — Choose where the text content appears on the banner (Left, Center, or Right). Default: Center.

docs.title: Heading
docs.text:
• Heading — The main headline text overlaid on your banner image. Default: "Banner title".
  • Heading size — Choose how large the heading appears (H1-size through Title 2-size). Default: H2-size.
  • Heading font-weight — Choose between Normal or Bold. Default: Bold.

docs.title: Subheading
docs.text:
• Subheading — Secondary text that appears below the heading. Use this for additional context or supporting information. Default: "A subheading for this banner".
  • Subheading font size — Choose the size for the subheading (H1-size through Title 2-size). Default: H6-size.
  • Subheading font-weight — Choose between Normal or Bold. Default: Normal.

docs.title: Button
docs.text:
Add a primary call-to-action button:

  • Button text — The text shown on the button. Leave empty to hide the button. Default: "Learn more".
  • Link — Where the button should take visitors when clicked.
  • Secondary button style — Enable to style the button as an outlined button instead of a solid button. Default: Disabled.
  • Button icon — Add an optional icon to the button (None, Chevron Right, Arrow Circle Right, or Arrow Right). (Only visible when button text is provided)

docs.title: Button 2
docs.text:
Add an optional second call-to-action button:

  • Button 2 text — The text for the second button. Leave empty to hide it. Default: "Another button".
  • Link — Where the second button should navigate.
  • Secondary button style — Enable to style button 2 as an outlined button. Default: Enabled.
  • Button 2 icon — Add an optional icon to the second button. (Only visible when button 2 text is provided)

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text: This section does not use blocks. All content is configured directly in the section settings above.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Image selection: Choose images with plenty of negative space (empty areas) where you plan to place your text. This ensures your heading and buttons remain readable.
  • Text contrast: Make sure your text color (from the color scheme) contrasts well with your image. If your image is dark, use a light text color, and vice versa.
  • Banner height: For homepage hero banners, taller heights (600-800px) create more impact. For interior pages, shorter heights (300-400px) work better.
  • Mobile considerations: Your banner will automatically adjust for mobile devices. Test how it looks on different screen sizes to ensure important elements aren't cut off.
  • Call to action: Use clear, action-oriented button text like "Shop Now," "Learn More," or "Get Started" rather than generic text like "Click Here."

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about working with sections in Shopify themes, visit Shopify's Help Center.

docs.title: Brands Section
docs.text:
The Brands section showcases the brands or manufacturers you carry in your store. Display them in either a carousel slider or a static grid layout, perfect for highlighting your brand partnerships or product lines.

This section works great on your homepage, collection pages, or a dedicated "Our Brands" page.

docs.title: Adding or Managing the Section
docs.text:
1. From your Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Themes
  2. Click Customize on your current theme
  3. Navigate to the page where you want brands to appear
  4. Click Add section and select Brands
  5. Configure the section settings and add brand blocks

docs.title: Colors & Layout
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the background color and text style for the section. Default: Scheme 1.
  • Alignment — Position content left, center, or right. Default: Center.

docs.title: Display Type
docs.text:
• Display type — Choose how brands appear:
  • Slider — Brands slide in a carousel (recommended for many brands)
  • Grid — Brands display in rows and columns (better for fewer brands)

Default: Grid.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
• Section type — Control the section width:
  • Container — Content stays within standard page width
  • Full width — Content stretches edge-to-edge

Default: Full width.

  • Section height — Set the background height behavior:
  • Auto — Background adjusts to content
  • Fixed — Background has a set height percentage

Default: Auto.

  • Section background height — If using Fixed height, set the background size. Range: 0-100%. Default: 80%. (Only visible when Section height is "Fixed")

docs.title: Grid Settings (Grid Display Only)
docs.text:
• Columns (mobile) — Number of brands per row on phones. Options: 1-4 columns. Default: 2.
  • Columns (tablet) — Number of brands per row on tablets. Options: 1-6 columns. Default: 3.
  • Columns (desktop) — Number of brands per row on desktop. Options: 1-8 columns. Default: 4.
  • Alternate offset — Enable to stagger every other brand slightly lower, creating a dynamic layout. Default: Disabled.

docs.title: Slider Settings (Slider Display Only)
docs.text:
• Slides per view (desktop) — How many brands show at once on desktop. Options: 2-8 slides. Default: 4.
  • Slides per view (tablet) — How many brands show at once on tablets. Options: 1-4.5 slides or Automatic. Default: 3.
  • Slides per view (phone) — How many brands show on mobile. Options: 1-4 slides or Automatic. Default: 2.
  • Carousel overflow — Enable to show a peek of the next brand, encouraging scrolling. Default: Disabled.
  • Slider pagination — Show dot indicators below the carousel for navigation. Default: Enabled.

docs.title: Brand Cards
docs.text:
• Image ratio — Control the aspect ratio of brand images:
  • Adapt to image — Use the original image dimensions
  • 1:1 — Square
  • 4:3 — Standard rectangle
  • 16:9 — Wide rectangle
  • 3:2 — Horizontal rectangle

Default: Adapt to image.

docs.title: Spacing
docs.text:
• Margin top — Space above the section. Options: Standard or None. Default: Standard.
  • Margin bottom — Space below the section. Options: Standard or None. Default: Standard.
  • Padding top — Inner spacing at the top. Options: Standard or None. Default: Standard.
  • Padding bottom — Inner spacing at the bottom. Options: Standard or None. Default: Standard.

docs.title: Content Settings
docs.text:
The section includes standard content blocks you can add:

  • Heading — Section title (e.g., "Our Brands")
  • Subheading — Additional descriptive text
  • Text — Paragraph content explaining your brand partnerships
  • Button — Call-to-action button (e.g., "View All Brands")

See the Content Section documentation for details on using these content blocks.

docs.title: Brand Block
docs.text:
Add brand blocks to display individual brand logos or images. You can add as many brands as you need.

Settings for each Brand:

  • Image — Upload the brand's logo or representative image. For best results, use square images or images with transparent backgrounds.

  • Link — Optional URL where customers go when clicking the brand. Common options:

  • Link to a collection filtered by that brand
  • Link to an external brand website

  • Leave empty for no link

  • Heading — Brand name (appears below the logo). Supports inline rich text.

  • Text — Optional description or tagline for the brand.

Note: Each brand block represents one brand. Add multiple blocks to show multiple brands.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Logo quality: Use high-resolution brand logos with transparent backgrounds for the best appearance.

  • Consistent sizing: Try to use brand logos of similar sizes and orientations. Square or horizontal logos work best.

  • Slider vs. Grid:

  • Use Slider if you have 8+ brands to avoid overwhelming the page

  • Use Grid if you have 4-8 brands you want all visible at once

  • Link strategy: Link brands to collections filtered by that brand, making it easy for customers to shop specific manufacturers.

  • Authorization: Make sure you have permission to use brand logos. Some brands provide partner assets for retailers.

  • Mobile layout: Brands automatically stack more vertically on mobile. Test to ensure logos remain clear at smaller sizes.

  • Alternate offset: This creates visual interest in grid layouts, but works best with uniform brand logos.

  • Brand page: Consider creating a dedicated page (like "Our Brands" or "Shop by Manufacturer") where you showcase all your brands with this section.

  • Homepage placement: The brands section works well near the bottom of your homepage, building trust by showing reputable brands you carry.

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
• Homepage: Display top or featured brands your store carries
  • About page: Show brand partnerships and affiliations
  • Brand page: Dedicated page listing all available brands with links to filter collections
  • Collection pages: Showcase brands within a specific category
  • Trust building: Use recognizable brand logos to build credibility with new customers

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about organizing products by brand, visit: - Product organization best practices - Creating filtered collections

docs.title: Breadcrumbs Section
docs.text:
The Breadcrumbs section displays a navigation path showing customers where they are within your store's hierarchy. It helps with both navigation and SEO by showing the page structure.

Breadcrumbs appear automatically on most pages (except the homepage and 404 page) and show the path from home to the current page.

docs.title: What Are Breadcrumbs?
docs.text:
Breadcrumbs are a navigation aid that shows the current page's location in the site hierarchy. They typically look like:

Home > Collections > Women's Clothing > Summer Dresses

Customers can click any part of the breadcrumb trail to navigate back up the hierarchy.

docs.title: Adding or Managing the Section
docs.text:
1. From your Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Themes
  2. Click Customize on your current theme
  3. Navigate to any page (not the homepage)
  4. Look for the Breadcrumbs section near the top of the page
  5. Click on it to adjust settings

Note: Breadcrumbs automatically appear on all pages except the homepage and 404 page. You don't need to manually add them to each page.

docs.title: Colors
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the background color and text style for the breadcrumbs. Default: Scheme 1.

That's it! Breadcrumbs are simple by design. The trail is automatically generated based on the page structure.

docs.title: How Breadcrumbs Work on Different Pages
docs.text: The breadcrumb trail changes automatically depending on the page type:

docs.title: Product Pages
docs.text:
Home > Collection Name > Product Name

If a customer arrived from a collection, that collection is included in the breadcrumb trail.

docs.title: Collection Pages
docs.text:
Home > Collection Name

If the collection has active tag filters: Home > Collection Name > Tag Name

docs.title: Blog Pages
docs.text:
Home > Blog Name

With tag filters: Home > Blog Name > Tag Name

docs.title: Article Pages
docs.text: Home > Blog Name > Article Title

docs.title: Regular Pages
docs.text: Home > Page Title

docs.title: Cart Page
docs.text: Home > Cart

docs.title: List Collections Page
docs.text: Home > Collections

docs.title: For Customers:
docs.text:
• Easy navigation — Quickly go back to higher-level pages
  • Context — Understand where they are in the site structure
  • Reduced clicks — Jump directly to any level in the hierarchy

docs.title: For Your Store:
docs.text:
• SEO improvement — Search engines use breadcrumbs to understand site structure
  • Lower bounce rate — Customers can easily explore related pages
  • Professional appearance — Shows site organization and attention to detail

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Styling: Choose a color scheme that contrasts subtly with your page background. Breadcrumbs should be visible but not dominate the page.

  • Mobile layout: Breadcrumbs automatically adjust for mobile devices. They may wrap to multiple lines if the path is long—this is normal.

  • Collection context: When customers browse from a collection to a product, the collection appears in the breadcrumb. This encourages them to return to browsing that collection.

  • SEO benefits: Keep breadcrumbs enabled for better search engine visibility. They help Google understand your site structure.

  • Position: Breadcrumbs typically appear near the top of the page, below the header but above the main content. This is the standard position customers expect.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Don't hide breadcrumbs: Unless you have a specific reason, keep breadcrumbs visible. They're a standard navigation element customers expect.

  • Page titles matter: Since breadcrumbs use your page titles, make sure titles are:

  • Clear and descriptive
  • Not too long (breadcrumbs can wrap awkwardly with very long titles)

  • Accurately represent the page content

  • Collection names: Use descriptive collection names like "Women's Shoes" rather than generic names like "Collection 1"—these appear in breadcrumbs.

  • Test the paths: Navigate through your store and verify breadcrumb trails make sense and help customers understand where they are.

  • Consistent structure: Organize your collections and products logically so breadcrumb trails reflect an intuitive hierarchy.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text:
Breadcrumbs include proper accessibility markup: - Wrapped in a <nav> element with role="navigation" - Include aria-label="breadcrumb" for screen readers - Mark the current page with aria-current="page"

This helps customers using assistive technologies navigate your store.

docs.title: Automatic Display
docs.text: Breadcrumbs are automatically: - Hidden on homepage (no breadcrumb needed) - Hidden on 404 pages (path doesn't apply) - Displayed on all other page types

docs.title: Dynamic Generation
docs.text:
The breadcrumb trail is generated dynamically based on: - Current page type and template - Collection context (if arriving from collection) - Active tags or filters - URL structure

You don't need to manually configure breadcrumbs for each page—the theme handles this automatically.

docs.title: Customizing Breadcrumb Text
docs.text:
While breadcrumb labels are mostly automatic, you can influence them by:

  • Collection titles — Edit in Products > Collections
  • Product titles — Edit in Products
  • Page titles — Edit in Online Store > Pages
  • Blog titles — Edit in Online Store > Blog Posts > Manage blogs
  • Article titles — Edit individual blog posts

Breadcrumbs use these titles directly, so clear, concise titles work best.

docs.title: Removing Breadcrumbs
docs.text:
If you want to remove breadcrumbs from your store:

  1. In the Theme Editor, navigate to any page where breadcrumbs appear
  2. Click on the Breadcrumbs section
  3. Click Remove section (trash icon)
  4. Save your changes

Note: Removing breadcrumbs impacts navigation and SEO. Only remove them if you have a specific reason.

docs.title: SEO Benefits
docs.text:
Breadcrumbs provide SEO value by: * Creating a clear site hierarchy for search engines * Generating additional internal links * Appearing in Google search results (breadcrumb markup) * Reducing bounce rate (easier navigation) * Improving page authority distribution

Most SEO experts recommend keeping breadcrumbs enabled for these benefits.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about navigation and site structure, visit: - Managing menus and navigation - SEO best practices - Organizing your store

docs.title: Collections Grid Section
docs.text:
The Collections Grid section displays your product collections in a clean, organized grid layout. Unlike the Collections carousel, this shows all collections at once in rows and columns without requiring scrolling.

Use this section to: - Display all your main collections on one screen - Create a visual directory of your product categories - Help customers browse your entire catalog - Organize collections by theme or category

docs.title: Adding and Managing This Section
docs.text: This section can be added to most pages in your store. To learn how to add, remove, or reorder sections on your page, please refer to Shopify's official guide on Using sections and blocks.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the color scheme for this section's background and text. Default: Scheme 1.
  • Margin top — Control the top margin. Choose between Auto or None.
  • Margin bottom — Control the bottom margin. Choose between Auto or None.
  • Padding top — Control the internal top padding. Choose between Auto or None.
  • Padding bottom — Control the internal bottom padding. Choose between Auto or None.

docs.title: Items Per Row
docs.text:
Control how many collections appear side-by-side on different devices:

  • Items per row (desktop) — Number of collections per row on desktop. Options: 3, 4, or 6 columns. Default: 4.
  • Items per row (tablet) — Number of collections per row on tablets. Options: 2, 3, or 4 columns. Default: 3.
  • Items per row (mobile) — Number of collections per row on mobile phones. Options: 2 or 3 columns. Default: 2.

docs.title: Section Settings
docs.text: • Collections — Select up to 20 collections to display. If you don't select any, the section will automatically show collections for you.

docs.title: Text Settings
docs.text:
• Text alignment — Choose Left, Center, or Right alignment for the heading and content. Default: Center.
  • Heading — The main heading for this section. Default: "Example heading".
  • Heading tag — Choose the HTML tag for SEO (H1, H2, H3, H4, H5, H6, or span). Default: H2.
  • Heading size — Choose the visual size (H1-size through Title 2-size). Default: H2-size.
  • Heading font-weight — Choose Normal or Bold. Default: Bold.
  • Content — Add descriptive text below the heading. Supports rich text.

docs.title: Button
docs.text:
Add an optional button:

  • Button text — The text shown on the button. Leave empty to hide.
  • Link — Where the button navigates. (Only visible when button text is provided)
  • Secondary button style — Enable for an outlined button style. Default: Disabled. (Only visible when button text is provided)
  • Button icon — Add an optional icon. (Only visible when button text is provided)

docs.title: Button 2
docs.text:
Add an optional second button:

  • Button 2 text — The text for the second button. Leave empty to hide.
  • Link — Where button 2 navigates. (Only visible when button 2 text is provided)
  • Secondary button style — Enable for an outlined button style. Default: Enabled. (Only visible when button 2 text is provided)
  • Button 2 icon — Add an optional icon. (Only visible when button 2 text is provided)

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text: This section does not use blocks. Collections are selected directly in the Collections setting.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Grid vs. Carousel: Use the grid when you want customers to see all your collections at once without interaction. Use the Collections carousel when you have many collections and want to save vertical space.

  • Collection selection: Manually select which collections to display for more control, or leave it empty to let the theme choose automatically.

  • Collection images: Make sure each collection has an attractive featured image set in Products > Collections in your Shopify admin. These images are crucial for visual appeal.

  • Desktop layout:

  • 4 columns works well for most stores (shows 8-12 collections without scrolling)
  • 3 columns works better for larger collection images

  • 6 columns is ideal when you have many small collections to display

  • Mobile considerations: On mobile, 2 columns usually provides the best experience. 3 columns can work for simpler collection images but may feel cramped.

  • Card appearance: The look of collection cards is controlled by global settings in Theme Settings > Collection & Brand Cards.

  • Strategic use: This section works great on:

  • A "Shop" or "Collections" landing page
  • Your homepage if you have 4-12 main collections

  • Category pages to show subcollections

  • Call to action: Use the buttons to provide additional navigation options, like "View All Products" or "New Arrivals".

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about managing collections in Shopify, visit: - Creating and managing collections - Working with sections

docs.title: Collections Section
docs.text:
The Collections section displays your product collections in a beautiful sliding carousel. This is perfect for showcasing multiple collections and encouraging customers to explore different parts of your store.

Use this section to: - Feature your main product collections on the homepage - Help customers discover different product categories - Organize products by theme, season, or type - Create visual navigation to your store's collections

docs.title: Adding and Managing This Section
docs.text: This section can be added to most pages in your store. To learn how to add, remove, or reorder sections on your page, please refer to Shopify's official guide on Using sections and blocks.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the color scheme for this section's background and text. Default: Scheme 2.
  • Margin top — Control the top margin (space above the section). Choose between Auto or None.
  • Margin bottom — Control the bottom margin (space below the section). Choose between Auto or None.
  • Padding top — Control the internal top padding within the section. Choose between Auto or None.
  • Padding bottom — Control the internal bottom padding within the section. Choose between Auto or None.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
• Section type — Choose the section width:
  • Edge to Edge — Section background extends to the screen edges
  • Box — Section stays within a container

Default: Box. * Section height — Choose how the section height is determined: - Fixed height — Section has a fixed height - Grow with content — Section height adjusts automatically

Default: Grow with content. * Background height — When using fixed height, control what percentage of the viewport the section fills. Range: 0-100%. Default: 80%. (Only visible when section height is set to Fixed)

docs.title: Section Settings
docs.text: • Collections — Select up to 20 collections to display in the carousel. If you don't select any collections, the first 20 collections from your store will automatically be displayed.

docs.title: Slider Settings
docs.text:
Control how the collections carousel behaves:

  • Slides per view (desktop) — How many collections to show at once on desktop. Options: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, or Automatic. Default: 4.
  • Slides per view (tablet) — How many collections to show on tablets. Options: 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5, or Automatic. Default: 3.
  • Slides per view (phone) — How many collections to show on phones. Options: 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, or Automatic. Default: 1.5.
  • Slider pagination bullets — Enable to show navigation dots below the carousel. Default: Disabled.
  • Alternate image offset — When enabled, every other collection card will be offset downward, creating a staggered visual effect. Default: Disabled.
  • Carousel outside container — When enabled, the carousel extends beyond the container width, allowing cards to peek from the sides. Default: Enabled.

docs.title: Text Settings
docs.text:
Options for the introductory text that appears above the collections:

  • Text alignment — Choose Left, Center, or Right alignment. Default: Center.
  • Heading — The main heading text that introduces the collections. Default: "Example heading".
  • Heading tag — Choose the HTML tag for SEO purposes (H1, H2, H3, H4, H5, H6, or span). Default: H2.
  • Heading size — Choose how large the heading appears visually. Default: H2-size.
  • Heading font-weight — Choose between Normal or Bold. Default: Bold.
  • Content — Add descriptive text below the heading. Supports rich text.

docs.title: Button
docs.text:
Add an optional button below your section heading:

  • Button text — The text shown on the button. Leave empty to hide the button.
  • Link — Where the button should navigate when clicked.
  • Secondary button style — Enable to style as an outlined button. Default: Disabled.
  • Button icon — Add an optional icon to the button.

docs.title: Button 2
docs.text:
Add an optional second button:

  • Button 2 text — The text for the second button. Leave empty to hide it.
  • Link — Where the second button should navigate.
  • Secondary button style — Enable to style as an outlined button. Default: Enabled.
  • Button 2 icon — Add an optional icon.

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text: This section does not use blocks. Collections are selected directly in the Collections setting.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Collection selection: If you don't select any collections, the section will automatically show your first 20 collections. For more control, manually select which collections to display.

  • Collection images: Each collection displays its featured image. Make sure your collections have attractive featured images set in Products > Collections in your Shopify admin.

  • Collection order: Manually selected collections display in the order you choose. Drag and drop them in the collection list to reorder.

  • Card appearance: The look of collection cards is controlled by global settings in Theme Settings > Collection & Brand Cards. This includes borders, hover effects, and whether collection names are shown.

  • Mobile experience: Showing 1.5 or 2.5 collections on mobile helps customers understand they can swipe to see more options.

  • Strategic placement: This section works great on your homepage to help customers quickly navigate to different product categories.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about managing collections in Shopify, visit: - Creating and managing collections - Working with sections

docs.title: Contact Form Section
docs.text:
The Contact Form section provides a flexible, customizable contact form for your store. You can add various form fields, customize the layout, and make it easy for customers to get in touch with you.

Use this section to: - Create a custom contact page - Collect customer inquiries and feedback - Gather leads with specific information - Provide customer support options - Build custom forms for different purposes

docs.title: Adding and Managing This Section
docs.text: This section can be added to most pages in your store. To learn how to add, remove, or reorder sections on your page, please refer to Shopify's official guide on Using sections and blocks.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the color scheme for the section background. Default: Scheme 2.
  • Card color scheme — Choose the color scheme specifically for the form container/card. Default: Scheme 1.
  • Section type — Choose the section width:
  • Edge to Edge — Section extends to screen edges
  • Box — Section stays within a container

Default: Box. * Margin top — Control the top margin. Choose between Auto or None. * Margin bottom — Control the bottom margin. Choose between Auto or None. * Padding top — Control the internal top padding. Choose between Auto or None. * Padding bottom — Control the internal bottom padding. Choose between Auto or None.

docs.title: Text Settings
docs.text:
• Text alignment — Choose Left, Center, or Right alignment for the section heading and text. Default: Left.
  • Heading — The main heading above the form. Default: "Contact".
  • Heading tag — Choose the HTML tag for SEO (H1, H2, H3, H4, H5, H6, or span). Default: span.
  • Heading size — Choose the visual size for the heading. Default: H3-size.
  • Heading font-weight — Choose Normal or Bold. Default: Bold.
  • Intro Text — Add introductory text that appears above the form, explaining why customers should contact you or what to expect. Supports rich text.

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text: Build your form by adding different block types. Each block represents a form field or element.

docs.title: Heading Block
docs.text:
Add a heading within the form (different from the main section heading).

Settings: * Heading — The heading text. Default: "Contact Us". * Heading Tag — Choose the HTML tag (H1-H6 or span). Default: span. * Heading Size — Choose the visual size. Default: H3-size. * Heading font-weight — Choose Normal or Bold. Default: Bold.

docs.title: Name Input Block
docs.text:
Add a name field to your form. Limited to one per form.

Settings: * Required — Enable to make this field mandatory. Default: Disabled.

docs.title: Email Input Block
docs.text:
Add an email address field to your form. Limited to one per form.

This block has no additional settings — it's automatically configured as an email input.

docs.title: Input Field Block
docs.text:
Add a custom text input field. You can add multiple input blocks for different information.

Settings: * Name — The internal field name (used for form processing). Default: "unique_field_name". Make this unique for each field. * Label — The label shown to customers above the field. Default: "Your input". * Input Placeholder — Placeholder text shown inside the empty field. Default: "Enter your input". * Required — Enable to make this field mandatory. Default: Disabled. * Input Type — Choose the type of input: - Text — Regular text input - Email — Email address (with validation) - Phone — Phone number - Number — Numeric input only

docs.title: Message Input Block (Textarea)
docs.text:
Add a large text area for longer messages or comments.

Settings: * Required — Enable to make this field mandatory. Default: Disabled. * Textarea Rows — Control how tall the text area is. Range: 2-10 rows. Default: 4 rows.

docs.title: Submit Button Block
docs.text:
Add the form submit button. Limited to one per form.

Settings: * Button Text — The text shown on the submit button. Default: "Submit". * Button Icon — Add an optional icon to the button (None, Chevron Right, Arrow Circle Right, or Arrow Right).

docs.title: Default Form Setup
docs.text:
When you add this section, it includes a ready-to-use contact form with: - Heading: "Get in Touch" - Name field (required) - Email field - Phone field (optional) - Message textarea (required) - Submit button: "Send Message"

You can customize this by adding, removing, or rearranging blocks.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Required fields: Mark essential fields as required to ensure you get the information you need. At minimum, make email and message fields required.

  • Field names: When adding custom Input Field blocks, give each one a unique name (e.g., "company", "subject", "order_number"). This helps you identify the information when you receive form submissions.

  • Form submissions: Form submissions are sent to the email address specified in your Shopify admin under Settings > General > Store contact email.

  • Privacy note: If you collect personal information, mention your privacy policy in the intro text. This builds trust and may be legally required in some regions.

  • Keep it simple: Don't ask for too much information. The more fields you add, the less likely customers are to complete the form. Focus on essential fields only.

  • Mobile friendly: The form automatically adjusts for mobile devices. Test it on different screen sizes to ensure a good experience.

  • Custom forms: Use this section to create specialized forms beyond basic contact:

  • Wholesale inquiry forms (with company name, tax ID, etc.)
  • Custom order request forms
  • Partnership inquiry forms
  • Product feedback forms

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about working with forms in Shopify, visit: - Contact form setup - Working with sections

docs.title: Content Section
docs.text:
The Content section is the most flexible and powerful section in your theme. It allows you to build completely custom layouts using a variety of content blocks like titles, text, images, buttons, and columns. Think of it as a blank canvas where you can create unique page designs.

Use this section to: - Create custom "About Us" or "Our Story" pages - Build image and text layouts in any combination - Design custom landing pages - Add rich content between other sections - Create multi-column layouts with mixed content

docs.title: Adding and Managing This Section
docs.text: This versatile section can be added to any page in your store. To learn how to add, remove, or reorder sections on your page, please refer to Shopify's official guide on Using sections and blocks.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the color scheme for this section's background and text. Default: Scheme 2.
  • Margin top — Control the top margin (space above the section). Choose between Standard or None.
  • Margin bottom — Control the bottom margin (space below the section). Choose between Standard or None.
  • Padding top — Control the internal top padding within the section. Choose between Standard or None.
  • Padding bottom — Control the internal bottom padding within the section. Choose between Standard or None.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
• Section type — Choose the section width:
  • Container — Content stays within the content area with margins
  • Full width — Content extends edge-to-edge

Default: Container. * Section height — Choose how the section height is determined: - Auto — Section height adjusts automatically based on content - Fixed — Section has a fixed height * Section background height — When using fixed height, control what percentage of the viewport the section fills. Range: 0-100%. Default: 80%. (Only visible when section height is set to Fixed)

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text: This section is built entirely with blocks. You can add, remove, and rearrange blocks to create your perfect layout. The section accepts both theme blocks and app blocks.

docs.title: Available Block Types
docs.text:
The Content section can use any of the following block types:

  • Title — Add a heading with customizable size, weight, and color
  • Text — Add paragraphs or rich text content
  • Image — Add images with optional links
  • Button — Add clickable buttons (primary or secondary style)
  • Columns — Create multi-column layouts to organize other blocks
  • Column — Individual column blocks (used inside the Columns block)
  • Group — Group multiple blocks together for easier organization
  • FAQ — Add frequently asked questions with expandable answers

Each block type has its own settings that let you customize its appearance and behavior. Simply add a block to see its available options.

docs.title: Working with Columns
docs.text:
The Columns and Column blocks are powerful tools for creating side-by-side layouts:

  1. Add a Columns block to create a row
  2. Inside the Columns block, add individual Column blocks
  3. Inside each Column block, add your content (titles, text, images, buttons, etc.)

This lets you create layouts like: - Image on left, text on right - Text on left, image on right - Three columns of text - Any custom combination you can imagine

docs.title: Pre-made Layouts
docs.text:
When you add the Content section, you can choose from several ready-made layouts:

  • Heading — A simple large heading, perfect for introducing a page
  • Heading with text — Heading on the left, descriptive text on the right
  • Text with image — Text content on the left, image on the right
  • Text with image (reversed) — Image on the left, text on the right
  • Two images — Two side-by-side images

You can use these as starting points and then customize them by adding, removing, or rearranging blocks.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Start with a preset: Choose a pre-made layout that's close to what you want, then customize it to save time.
  • Alignment matters: Use the Column block's alignment settings to control whether content is centered, aligned to the top, or aligned to the bottom.
  • Mobile layout: Content automatically stacks vertically on mobile devices for better readability.
  • Nested blocks: Remember that some blocks (like Columns) contain other blocks. Click into them to add content.
  • Experiment freely: You can always undo changes or delete blocks if something doesn't look right.

docs.title: Advanced: Understanding the Grid System
docs.text:
The Column blocks use a 12-column grid system (common in web design): - 12/12 (col-12) = Full width - 6/12 (col-6) = Half width (2 columns side-by-side) - 4/12 (col-4) = One third width (3 columns side-by-side) - 3/12 (col-3) = One quarter width (4 columns side-by-side)

You can set different column widths for desktop, tablet, and mobile to create responsive layouts that look great on all devices.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about working with sections and blocks in Shopify themes, visit Shopify's Help Center.

docs.title: Footer Section
docs.text:
The Footer section appears at the bottom of every page on your store. It's a crucial place for navigation, legal links, newsletter signups, and social media connections. You can customize it with multiple columns containing different types of content.

Use the footer to: - Provide quick navigation to important pages - Display social media links - Collect newsletter subscribers - Share store information (hours, location, contact details) - Display legal links (Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, etc.)

docs.title: Adding and Managing This Section
docs.text:
The footer is a permanent section that appears on all pages. You can customize it through the Theme Editor by clicking on the footer section at the bottom of any page.

To learn more about working with sections and blocks in Shopify themes, please refer to Shopify's official guide on Using sections and blocks.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the color scheme for the footer background and text. Default: Scheme 2.
  • Section type — Choose the footer width:
  • Edge to Edge — Footer spans the full width of the screen
  • Box — Footer stays within a container with side margins

Default: Box. * Show policy links — Enable to automatically display links to your store policies (Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, Refund Policy, etc.). These are managed in your Shopify admin under Settings > Policies. Default: Disabled.

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text: The footer is built with blocks that create columns of content. You can add up to 8 navigation or content blocks, plus one social media and newsletter block.

docs.title: Socials & Newsletter Block
docs.text:
This special block combines social media links and a newsletter signup form. You can only add one of these blocks.

Social Media Settings: * Color scheme — Choose the color scheme specifically for this block. Default: Scheme 1. * Heading — The heading above your social media icons. Default: "Social media". * Heading font-weight — Choose Normal or Bold. Default: Bold. * Content — Add descriptive text encouraging visitors to follow you. Default: "Follow us on social media". Supports rich text.

Newsletter Settings: * Heading — The heading above the newsletter signup form. Default: "Newsletter". * Heading font-weight — Choose Normal or Bold. Default: Bold. * Content — Explain the benefits of subscribing. Default includes privacy policy mention. Supports rich text.

Note: The actual social media links are managed in your theme settings under Social Media. The icons displayed here reflect those settings.

docs.title: Navigation Block
docs.text:
Add navigation menus to create footer columns with links. You can add up to 8 of these blocks.

Settings: * Heading — The title for this navigation column. Default: "Navigation". * Navigation menu — Select which menu to display in this column. Default: Footer menu. You create and manage these menus in your Shopify admin under Navigation.

docs.title: Content Block
docs.text:
Add custom text content to create informational footer columns. You can add up to 8 of these blocks.

Settings: * Heading — The title for this content column. Default: "Our shop". * Content — Add any information you want to share (store hours, address, contact info, etc.). Default: "Open every weekday from 09:00 to 18:00". Supports rich text.

docs.title: Default Footer Layout
docs.text:
When you first add the footer section, it includes: - 1 Social & Newsletter block - 4 Navigation blocks

You can customize this by adding, removing, or rearranging blocks to suit your needs.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Footer organization: A common footer structure uses 4-5 columns:
  • Column 1: About/company info
  • Column 2: Customer service links
  • Column 3: Product categories
  • Column 4: Legal/policies

  • Column 5: Social & newsletter

  • Navigation menus: Create clear, focused menus for your footer in Shopify admin (Online Store > Navigation). Keep each menu to 5-8 links for readability.

  • Newsletter privacy: Always mention your privacy policy when collecting email addresses. This builds trust and may be required by law in some regions.

  • Mobile layout: Footer columns automatically stack vertically on mobile devices for easy reading.

  • Policy links: Enable "Show policy links" to automatically add your store policies. Make sure you've set these up in Shopify admin under Settings > Policies first.

  • Social media: Update your social media links in Theme Settings > Social Media. Any links you leave empty won't show icons in the footer.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about managing menus and navigation in Shopify, visit: - Managing menus - Setting up store policies

docs.title: Header Main Section
docs.text:
The Header Main section is the primary navigation bar that appears at the top of every page on your store. It contains your logo, main navigation menu, search functionality, and cart icon.

This is a core section of your theme that provides the main navigation structure for your entire store.

docs.title: Important Note
docs.text: The header is a permanent section that appears on all pages. You customize it through the Theme Editor by clicking on the header area at the top of any page. Any changes you make will apply across your entire store.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the color scheme for the header background and text. Default: Scheme 1.
  • Navigation color scheme — Choose the color scheme specifically for the navigation menu (dropdown menus). Default: Scheme 1.
  • Header type — Choose the header size:
  • Small — Compact header with less padding
  • Large — Spacious header with more breathing room

Default: Large. * Font size — Control the size of text in the header. Range: 10-20px. Default: 16px. * Shadow — Enable to add a subtle shadow below the header, making it stand out from the page content. Default: Enabled.

docs.title: Brand
docs.text:
• Brand name — Enter your store or brand name to display next to your logo. Default: "Inspire". Supports inline rich text.
  • Hide brand name on mobile — Enable to hide the brand name text on mobile devices (your logo will still show). Default: Disabled.

Note: Your logo is configured in Theme Settings > Logo, not in this section.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
• Search suggestions — Select a menu to show as quick search suggestions when customers use the search bar. Create this menu in your Shopify admin under Navigation.
  • Slides per view (desktop) — Control how many search suggestions show at once in the search dropdown. Options: 3, 4, or 5 suggestions. Default: 4.

docs.title: Navigation Menu
docs.text:
Your main navigation menu is set up in your Shopify admin under Online Store > Navigation. The header automatically displays the menu you've assigned as your "Main menu."

To customize your navigation: 1. Go to Shopify admin > Online Store > Navigation 2. Click on "Main menu" 3. Add, remove, or reorder menu items 4. Create dropdown menus by nesting items under parent items

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Keep navigation simple: Aim for 5-7 main menu items. Too many options can overwhelm visitors.

  • Use dropdowns wisely: Create dropdown menus for collections or categories, but don't nest more than 2 levels deep.

  • Search suggestions: Set up a menu with your most popular collections or products to help customers find what they're looking for faster.

  • Mobile header: The header automatically adapts for mobile, showing a hamburger menu icon. Test it on mobile devices to ensure everything works well.

  • Sticky header: The header typically "sticks" to the top of the screen as customers scroll, keeping navigation always accessible.

  • Transparent header: You can enable a transparent header on your homepage in Theme Settings > Header. This works beautifully with full-width hero images.

  • Logo visibility: Make sure your logo has good contrast with your header background color for maximum visibility.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about managing your store's navigation, visit: - Managing menus and navigation - Customizing your header

docs.title: Header Top Section
docs.text:
The Header Top section (also called the "top bar") is a slim banner that sits above your main header. It's perfect for displaying unique selling points (USPs), promotional messages, or important announcements that scroll continuously.

This section is optional and appears at the very top of every page on your store.

docs.title: Adding or Managing the Section
docs.text:
1. From your Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Themes
  2. Click Customize on your current theme
  3. Navigate to any page
  4. Look for the Header Top section at the top of the page
  5. Click on it to edit settings or add USP blocks

docs.title: Colors & Styling
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the background color and text style for the top bar. Default: Scheme 2.
  • Font size — Control the size of text in the top bar. Range: 10-20px. Default: 14px.

docs.title: USP Block
docs.text:
Add up to 5 USP blocks to display rotating messages or selling points in the top bar.

Settings for each USP:

  • Icon — Enter a Font Awesome icon code to display before your text. Default: "fa-solid fa-check".
  • Examples: fa-solid fa-truck (shipping), fa-solid fa-shield (security), fa-solid fa-heart (satisfaction)

  • Find more icons at fontawesome.com

  • Text — Your USP message. Supports inline rich text formatting (bold, italic, links). Default: "Example Unique Selling Point".

docs.title: Language & Country Selector
docs.text:
The top bar automatically displays a language and country selector on the right side (desktop only) if you have multiple languages or markets enabled in your Shopify settings.

Customers can click the globe icon to: - Switch between available languages - Change their country/region and currency

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Keep it short: USPs should be brief and scannable since they scroll continuously. Aim for 3-5 words per message.

  • Highlight benefits: Focus on what matters to customers:

  • "Free Shipping Over $50"
  • "30-Day Returns"
  • "Secure Checkout"

  • "24/7 Customer Support"

  • Use icons strategically: Icons help messages stand out and communicate meaning instantly. Choose icons that clearly represent your message.

  • Limit the number: While you can add up to 5 USPs, 3-4 usually works best. Too many messages can feel overwhelming.

  • Mobile considerations: The top bar is visible on mobile, but only USPs show (no language selector on small screens).

  • Formatting: Use bold text sparingly to emphasize key words in your USP messages.

  • Consistent color scheme: Make sure your top bar contrasts well with your main header below it. Using a different color scheme can help it stand out.

  • Rotating messages: Messages automatically rotate in a carousel, so customers see all your USPs even if they don't scroll.

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
• Promotional periods: Announce sales, discount codes, or limited-time offers
  • Trust signals: Display security badges, guarantees, or certifications
  • Key benefits: Highlight free shipping, easy returns, fast delivery
  • Customer service: Share contact information or support availability
  • Social proof: Mention awards, ratings, or customer count

docs.title: Removing the Top Bar
docs.text:
If you don't want a top bar on your store:

  1. In the Theme Editor, click on the Header Top section
  2. Click the Remove section button (trash icon)
  3. Save your changes

You can always add it back later by clicking Add section in the header area.

docs.title: Banners Section
docs.text:
The Banners section (also called "Hero Cards") is perfect for showcasing collections, promotions, or featured content in an eye-catching way. You can display multiple banner cards either as a slider (carousel) or as a grid layout. Each banner includes an image, title, and clickable link.

Use this section to: - Feature your best-selling collections - Promote seasonal sales or special offers - Highlight brand stories or lifestyle imagery - Create visual navigation to different parts of your store

docs.title: Adding and Managing This Section
docs.text: This is a flexible section that can be added to most pages in your store. To learn how to add, remove, or reorder sections on your page, please refer to Shopify's official guide on Using sections and blocks.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the color scheme for the section background and text area. Default: Scheme 2.
  • Card color scheme — Choose the color scheme specifically for the banner cards themselves. Default: Scheme 1.
  • Margin top — Control the top margin (space above the section). Choose between Standard or None.
  • Margin bottom — Control the bottom margin (space below the section). Choose between Standard or None.
  • Padding top — Control the internal top padding within the section. Choose between Standard or None.
  • Padding bottom — Control the internal bottom padding within the section. Choose between Standard or None.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
• Section type — Choose whether the section spans the full width of the screen or stays within a container:
  • Full width — Section background extends edge-to-edge
  • Container — Section stays within the content area
  • Section height — Choose how the section height is determined:
  • Auto — Section height adjusts automatically based on content
  • Fixed — Section has a fixed height (use the next setting to control)
  • Background height — When using fixed height, control what percentage of the viewport the section fills. Range: 0-100%. Default: 80%. (Only visible when section height is set to Fixed)

docs.title: Display
docs.text:
• Display type — Choose how banners are displayed:
  • Slider — Banners appear in a carousel that users can scroll through
  • Grid — Banners appear in a static grid layout
  • Image Ratio — Control the shape of banner images:
  • 1:1 (Square)
  • 3:4 — Portrait (taller)
  • 4:3 — Landscape (wider)
  • 16:9 — Wide landscape
  • 9:16 — Tall portrait

Default: 3:4

docs.title: Grid Settings
docs.text:
These settings control the grid layout when "Display type" is set to Grid:

  • Grid columns (desktop) — Number of columns on desktop. Options: 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6. Default: 4.
  • Grid columns (tablet) — Number of columns on tablets. Options: 1, 2, 3, or 4. Default: 3.
  • Grid columns (mobile) — Number of columns on mobile phones. Options: 1, 2, or 3. Default: 2.

docs.title: Slider Settings
docs.text:
These settings control the carousel when "Display type" is set to Slider:

  • Slides per view — How many banners to show at once on desktop. Options: 2 through 8 slides. Default: 4.
  • Slides per view (tablet) — How many banners to show on tablets. Options include 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5, or Automatic. Default: 2.5.
  • Slides per view (phone) — How many banners to show on phones. Options: 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, or Automatic. Default: 1.5. (Decimal values like 1.5 show one full card plus a partial peek of the next)
  • Slider pagination bullets — Enable to show navigation dots below the slider. Default: Disabled.
  • Alternate image offset — When enabled, every other banner card will be offset downward, creating a staggered visual effect. Default: Disabled.
  • Carousel outside container — When enabled, the carousel extends beyond the container width, allowing cards to peek from the sides. Default: Enabled.

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
Options for the introductory text that appears above the banners:

  • Text alignment — Choose Left, Center, or Right alignment for the heading and content. Default: Center.
  • Heading — The main heading text that introduces the section. Default: "Example heading".
  • Select the HTML tag for the heading — Choose the HTML tag for SEO purposes (H1, H2, H3, H4, H5, H6, or span). This doesn't affect the visual size. Default: H2.
  • Heading size — Choose how large the heading appears (H1-size through Title 2-size). This doesn't affect the HTML tag, only the visual size. Default: H2-size.
  • Heading font-weight — Choose between Normal or Bold. Default: Bold.
  • Content — Add descriptive text or a paragraph below the heading. Supports rich text formatting.

docs.title: Button
docs.text:
Add an optional primary button below your section heading and content:

  • Button text — The text shown on the button. Leave empty to hide the button. Default: "Learn more".
  • Link — Where the button should navigate when clicked. (Only visible when button text is provided)
  • Button icon — Add an optional icon to the button (None, Chevron Right, Arrow Circle Right, or Arrow Right). (Only visible when button text is provided)
  • Secondary button style — Enable to style the button as an outlined secondary button instead of a solid primary button. Default: Disabled. (Only visible when button text is provided)

docs.title: Button 2
docs.text:
Add an optional second button next to your primary button:

  • Button 2 text — The text for the second button. Leave empty to hide it. Default: "Another button".
  • Link — Where the second button should navigate. (Only visible when button 2 text is provided)
  • Button 2 icon — Add an optional icon to the second button. (Only visible when button 2 text is provided)
  • Secondary button style — Enable to style button 2 as an outlined button. Default: Enabled. (Only visible when button 2 text is provided)

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text: This section uses Banner blocks. Add as many banner blocks as you need — each represents one clickable card in your grid or slider.

docs.title: Banner Block
docs.text:
Each banner block has the following settings:

  • Title — The text that appears overlaid on the banner image. Default: "Banner title".
  • Link — The URL where customers will be taken when they click the banner.
  • Image — Upload the banner image. Choose high-quality images that represent your collection or promotion.

Tip: For best results, use images with similar dimensions and color schemes for a cohesive look.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Slider vs. Grid: Use the slider when you have many banners and want to save vertical space. Use the grid when you want to show all options at once without requiring interaction.
  • Image dimensions: While the image ratio setting controls how images are cropped, try to upload images that match your chosen ratio to avoid important parts being cut off.
  • Mobile optimization: On mobile, showing 1.5 or 2.5 slides helps customers understand they can swipe to see more options.
  • Alternate offset: This works especially well with portrait images (3:4 or 9:16 ratios) to create visual interest.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about working with sections and blocks in Shopify themes, visit Shopify's Help Center.

docs.title: Icons Section
docs.text:
The Icons section (also known as "Features" or "USPs") lets you highlight key selling points, benefits, or features using icon cards. This is perfect for quickly communicating what makes your store special.

Use this section to: - Highlight unique selling points (free shipping, easy returns, etc.) - Showcase product or service features - Display trust badges and guarantees - Communicate key benefits at a glance - Build confidence with customers

docs.title: Adding and Managing This Section
docs.text: This section can be added to most pages in your store. To learn how to add, remove, or reorder sections on your page, please refer to Shopify's official guide on Using sections and blocks.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• No margin bottom — Enable to remove the bottom margin and place this section directly against the next section. Default: Disabled.
  • Color scheme — Choose the color scheme for this section's background and text. Default: Scheme 1.
  • Margin top — Control the top margin. Choose between Standard or None.
  • Margin bottom — Control the bottom margin. Choose between Standard or None.
  • Padding top — Control the internal top padding. Choose between Standard or None.
  • Padding bottom — Control the internal bottom padding. Choose between Standard or None.

docs.title: Icon Block
docs.text:
Add as many icon blocks as you need. Each block displays an icon with a heading and descriptive text.

Settings:

Icon: * Icon — Enter the Font Awesome icon code for the icon you want to display. Default: "fa-regular fa-star". - Visit Font Awesome to browse free icons - Copy the icon code (e.g., "fa-solid fa-truck-fast" for a delivery truck) - Paste it into this field

Text: * Heading — The title for this feature or benefit. Default: "Lorem Ipsum Dolor". * Text — The descriptive text explaining this feature. Default: "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit." Supports inline rich text.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Common use cases: This section is perfect for:
  • Free Shipping (use a truck icon: fa-solid fa-truck-fast)
  • Secure Payment (use a lock icon: fa-solid fa-lock)
  • Easy Returns (use a return arrow: fa-solid fa-rotate-left)
  • 24/7 Support (use a headset icon: fa-solid fa-headset)

  • Quality Guarantee (use a badge icon: fa-solid fa-certificate)

  • Finding icons:

  • Go to fontawesome.com/search
  • Search for what you need (e.g., "delivery", "secure", "support")
  • Click on an icon you like
  • Copy the full code (e.g., fa-solid fa-truck-fast)

  • Paste it into the Icon field

  • Icon styles: Font Awesome offers different icon styles:

  • fa-solid — Filled/solid icons (most common)
  • fa-regular — Outlined/regular icons

  • Choose the style that matches your design

  • Keep text brief: Each icon block should communicate one clear benefit. Keep headings short (2-4 words) and descriptions concise (one sentence).

  • Number of icons: 3-4 icons works well for most layouts, but you can add more. The icons automatically arrange into rows based on screen size.

  • Placement: This section works great:

  • Just below your hero image on the homepage
  • Above the footer as a reassurance banner

  • On product pages to highlight key features

  • Mobile layout: Icons automatically stack vertically on mobile devices for easy reading.

docs.title: Default Setup
docs.text: When you add this section, it includes 4 sample icon blocks with star icons. Replace these with your own icons and content to match your store's unique selling points.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about working with sections in Shopify themes, visit Shopify's Help Center.

docs.title: Image Carousel Section
docs.text:
The Image Carousel section creates a full-width or contained image slider perfect for showcasing multiple images or videos with text overlays and call-to-action buttons. It's ideal for highlighting multiple products, promotions, or brand storytelling.

Think of it as an advanced hero section that slides through multiple images or videos.

docs.title: Adding or Managing the Section
docs.text:
1. From your Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Themes
  2. Click Customize on your current theme
  3. Navigate to the page where you want the carousel
  4. Click Add section and select Image Carousel
  5. Configure section settings and add image or video slides

docs.title: Colors & Display
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the background color for the section container. Default: Scheme 1.
  • Slide color scheme — Choose the color scheme for text overlays on each slide. Default: Scheme 1.

docs.title: Width & Size
docs.text:
• Width type — Choose the carousel width:
  • Full width — Stretches edge-to-edge across the entire screen
  • Box — Contained within standard page width

Default: Box.

docs.title: Box Mode Settings (Only for Box Width)
docs.text:
• Image ratio — Control the aspect ratio of slides:
  • 1:1 — Square
  • 4:3 — Standard rectangle
  • 16:9 — Wide rectangle (great for banners)
  • 8:3 — Extra wide (cinematic)

Default: 8:3.

docs.title: Full Width Mode Settings (Only for Full Width)
docs.text: • Height — Set the fixed height of the carousel in pixels. Range: 200-1000px. Default: 600px.

docs.title: Carousel Behavior
docs.text:
• Loop — Enable to make the carousel loop continuously (after the last slide, return to the first). Default: Enabled.

  • Autoplay — Enable to automatically advance slides without user interaction. Default: Disabled.

  • Autoplay delay — If autoplay is enabled, set how long each slide displays (in milliseconds). Range: 1000-10000ms (1-10 seconds). Default: 5000ms (5 seconds).

docs.title: Overlay
docs.text:
• Background overlay — Add a color overlay on top of images/videos to improve text readability. Use format: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3) where the last number (0.3) controls opacity. Default: No overlay.

Tip: A dark overlay like rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4) helps white text stand out on light images.

docs.title: Spacing
docs.text:
• Margin top — Space above the section. Options: Standard or None. Default: Standard.
  • Margin bottom — Space below the section. Options: Standard or None. Default: None.
  • Padding top — Inner spacing at the top. Options: Standard or None. Default: Standard.
  • Padding bottom — Inner spacing at the bottom. Options: Standard or None. Default: Standard.

docs.title: Image Slide Block
docs.text:
Add image slides to your carousel. Each slide can have an image, text overlay, and button.

Settings:

  • Image — Upload the slide image. Recommended dimensions depend on your width setting:
  • Box mode: Match your theme's container width (typically 1200-1400px wide)

  • Full width mode: Use large images (at least 1920px wide)

  • Alignment — Position the text overlay:

  • Left — Text aligned to the left
  • Center — Text centered (recommended)
  • Right — Text aligned to the right

Default: Center.

Heading: * Heading — Main title text. Supports inline rich text. Default: "Slide title". * Heading size — Choose text size from H1-H6 or Title 1-2. Default: H2. * Heading font weight — Normal or Bold. Default: Bold.

Subheading: * Subheading — Secondary text below the heading. Supports inline rich text. Default: "A subheading for this slide". * Subheading font size — Choose text size from H1-H6 or Title 1-2. Default: H6. * Subheading font weight — Normal or Bold. Default: Normal.

Button: * Button text — Text displayed on the button. Leave empty to hide the button. Default: "Learn more". * Button link — URL where the button leads. Required if button text is entered. * Button icon — Optional Font Awesome icon to display in the button (e.g., fa-solid fa-arrow-right). * Button style — Choose the button appearance: - Primary — Solid colored button (most prominent) - Secondary — Outlined button - Link — Simple text link

Default: Primary.

docs.title: Video Slide Block
docs.text:
Add video slides to your carousel. Videos can autoplay and loop.

Settings:

  • Video — Upload a video file from your computer. Shopify supports MP4, MOV, and other common formats.

  • Autoplay — Enable to automatically play the video when the slide appears (recommended for background videos). Default: Enabled.

Note: When autoplay is disabled, video controls appear so customers can play/pause the video.

Text and button settings: Video slides support the same heading, subheading, and button options as image slides (see above).

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Number of slides: Aim for 3-5 slides. Too many can overwhelm visitors, while too few might not warrant a carousel.

  • Image quality: Use high-resolution images (at least 1920px wide for full-width carousels) to ensure crisp display on large screens.

  • Text readability: If text is hard to read over images:

  • Add a background overlay (use rgba color with transparency)
  • Use images with clear areas for text placement

  • Adjust text alignment to avoid busy image areas

  • Consistent styling: Keep heading sizes, colors, and button styles consistent across slides for a professional look.

  • Autoplay considerations:

  • Enable autoplay if slides are primarily visual and don't contain much text to read

  • Disable autoplay if slides have important text content customers need time to read

  • Video slides:

  • Keep videos short (10-30 seconds)
  • Use videos without sound (they auto-mute anyway)

  • Ensure videos work as background elements, not the main focus

  • Mobile optimization: Carousels automatically adapt for mobile. Test to ensure:

  • Text remains readable at small sizes
  • Buttons are easy to tap

  • Images don't lose important content when cropped
