  • Call-to-action: Each slide should have a clear purpose. Use the button to guide customers toward the desired action (shop now, learn more, etc.).

  • Slide order: Put your most important message or offer in the first slide—many visitors won't advance through the carousel.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Homepage hero: Use the image carousel as your main homepage banner to showcase multiple promotions or product categories.

  • Seasonal promotions: Update slides regularly to reflect current sales, seasons, or new arrivals.

  • Product launches: Dedicate slides to new product launches with compelling imagery and "Shop Now" buttons.

  • Brand storytelling: Use the carousel to tell your brand story across multiple slides.

  • A/B testing: Try different images, text, and calls-to-action to see what resonates with your customers.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about creating effective hero sections and carousels, visit: - Online store design tips - Image requirements and recommendations

docs.title: 404 Error Page Template
docs.text:
The 404 Error Page appears when customers try to access a page that doesn't exist on your store. This template helps you create a helpful, branded 404 experience that guides customers back to shopping instead of leaving your site.

A well-designed 404 page turns a frustrating experience into an opportunity to keep customers engaged.

docs.title: Important Note
docs.text: This template only appears when customers land on a non-existent page. You customize it by: 1. Going to your Theme Editor 2. In the page selector, choose 404 or type a random URL that doesn't exist 3. Adjusting the 404 page section settings

docs.title: Colors & Layout
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the background color and text style for the 404 page. Default: Scheme 1.

  • Section type — Control the content width:

  • Container — Content stays within standard page width (recommended)
  • Box — Full width display

Default: Container.

docs.title: Spacing
docs.text:
• Margin top — Space above the section. Options: Auto or None. Default: Auto.
  • Margin bottom — Space below the section. Options: Auto or None. Default: Auto.
  • Padding top — Inner spacing at the top. Options: Auto or None. Default: Auto.
  • Padding bottom — Inner spacing at the bottom. Options: Auto or None. Default: Auto.

docs.title: Default Page Elements
docs.text:
The 404 page automatically includes: * Question mark icon — Large icon (Font Awesome fa-circle-question) indicating something went wrong * Content blocks — You can add custom content using theme blocks (see below)

Everything is center-aligned for a clean, focused appearance.

docs.title: Blocks
docs.text: You can add theme blocks to customize the 404 page content:

docs.title: Common Blocks to Add
docs.text:
• Title block — Add a heading like "Page Not Found" or "Oops! Lost?"
  • Text block — Explain what happened and what customers can do next
  • Button blocks — Direct customers to:
  • Homepage
  • Shop page
  • Search page
  • Popular collections
  • Contact page

docs.title: Example 404 Content Structure
docs.text:
1. Title: "Page Not Found"
  2. Text: "Sorry, the page you're looking for doesn't exist. It may have been moved or deleted."
  3. Button 1: "Return to Homepage"
  4. Button 2: "Browse Collections"
  5. Button 3: "Search Products"

docs.title: Common Causes of 404 Errors
docs.text: Customers see 404 errors when they: * Click broken or outdated links * Mistype a URL * Follow old bookmarks to deleted pages * Click links from external sites that are incorrect * Access URLs from old marketing materials * Try URLs before you've published the page

docs.title: Content
docs.text:
• Be friendly, not technical — Avoid jargon like "404 error" or "page not found." Use conversational language like "Oops! We can't find that page."

  • Apologize briefly — A simple "Sorry about that" acknowledges the frustration without dwelling on it.

  • Offer solutions — Tell customers what they can do:

  • Return to the homepage
  • Use the search function
  • Browse popular categories

  • Contact support if they need help

  • Keep it lighthearted — Inject personality. This is a chance to show your brand voice and keep the mood positive.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Stay on-brand — Use your brand colors, fonts, and style. The 404 page should feel like part of your store.

  • Visual element — The default question mark icon works, or you could replace it with:

  • Custom illustration
  • Animated element

  • Relevant image from your catalog

  • Clear navigation — Make it obvious where customers can go next. Buttons should stand out.

  • Mobile-friendly — Test on mobile devices. Many 404 visits happen on phones.

docs.title: Functionality
docs.text:
• Working links — Ensure all buttons and links on your 404 page work correctly.

  • Search option — Include search functionality so customers can look for what they wanted.

  • Popular links — Link to your most-visited pages or best-selling collections.

docs.title: Reducing 404 Errors
docs.text: To minimize how often customers see this page:

docs.title: Set Up Redirects
docs.text:
When you delete or rename pages, products, or collections: 1. Go to Online Store > Navigation > URL Redirects 2. Add a redirect from the old URL to the new one 3. Save

This ensures old links automatically send customers to the right place.

docs.title: Check for Broken Links
docs.text: Regularly: * Review your navigation menus * Check footer links * Test links in email campaigns * Verify links on external sites and social media * Update printed materials with current URLs

docs.title: Monitor 404 Errors
docs.text: Use Shopify analytics or Google Search Console to: * See which non-existent pages customers are trying to access * Identify patterns (e.g., many people looking for /sale) * Create those popular pages or redirect to alternatives * Fix systematic issues (like broken menu links)

docs.title: Friendly and Helpful
docs.text:
Title: "Oops! Page Not Found"

Text: "We couldn't find the page you're looking for. It might have been moved, or perhaps there's a typo in the URL. Don't worry—we'll help you get back on track!"

Buttons: - Back to Homepage - Shop All Products - Contact Us

docs.title: Branded and Playful
docs.text:
Title: "404: Fashion Faux Pas"

Text: "Looks like this page is out of stock... permanently. But don't worry, we have plenty of other styles you'll love!"

Buttons: - Shop New Arrivals - View Bestsellers - Browse Collections

docs.title: Simple and Direct
docs.text:
Title: "Page Not Available"

Text: "The page you requested doesn't exist or has been moved. Try searching for what you need, or explore our collections."

Buttons: - Search Products - View Collections - Go Home

docs.title: Template Limitations
docs.text:
The 404 template is automatically triggered by Shopify when: * URL doesn't match any existing page * Product or collection has been deleted * URL is mistyped

You cannot create multiple 404 page variants—there's one 404 template for the entire store.

docs.title: SEO Considerations
docs.text:
• 404 pages return an HTTP 404 status code (correct for SEO)
  • Search engines won't index 404 pages
  • Too many 404 errors can impact SEO rankings
  • Use redirects instead of letting pages 404 when possible

docs.title: Add Search
docs.text:
Include a search bar directly on the 404 page using a custom HTML block:

<form action="/search" method="get">
  <input type="text" name="q" placeholder="Search our store...">
  <button type="submit">Search</button>
</form>

docs.title: Show Popular Products
docs.text: Add a product carousel or grid featuring bestsellers, giving customers immediate shopping options.

docs.title: Include Contact Information
docs.text: Add contact details or a link to customer support for customers who are truly lost.

docs.title: Humor and Brand Personality
docs.text: Use clever copy that reflects your brand: * Fashion store: "This outfit (URL) is no longer in our collection" * Tech store: "Error 404: Page.exe not found" * Food store: "This recipe has been taken off the menu"

docs.title: Testing Your 404 Page
docs.text:
To preview your 404 page:

  1. In the Theme Editor, select 404 from the page dropdown
  2. Or visit: your-store.myshopify.com/404 in a browser
  3. Test all buttons and links
  4. Check appearance on desktop, tablet, and mobile
  5. Verify content is helpful and on-brand

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about 404 pages and redirects, visit: - Setting up URL redirects - Finding broken links - SEO best practices

docs.title: Article Page Template
docs.text: The Article Page template displays individual blog posts with full content, featured images, author information, and social sharing options. This is where customers read your blog articles in detail.

docs.title: Colors & Layout
docs.text: • Color scheme — Background color and text style. Default: Scheme 1.

docs.title: Article Image
docs.text:
• Image width — Control featured image width:
  • Container — Image stays within page width
  • Box — Image stretches full width (edge-to-edge)

Default: Box.

  • Image height — Featured image height in pixels. Range: 300-800px. Default: 500px.

docs.title: Heading
docs.text:
• Heading tag — HTML tag for article title (H1-H6 or Span). Default: H1.
  • Heading size — Visual size of the title (Title 1, Title 2, or H1-H6). Default: H1.
  • Heading font weight — Text thickness (100-900). Default: 700.

docs.title: Content Width
docs.text:
• Container width — Maximum width for article text:
  • Default — Uses theme's standard container width
  • Custom — Set a specific width (Range: 600-1200px)

Default: Default.

Tip: Narrower content (around 700-800px) improves readability for long-form articles.

docs.title: Article Info
docs.text: • Show author — Display author name and publication date below title. Default: Enabled.

docs.title: Reading Experience
docs.text:
• Enable progress bar — Show reading progress indicator at top of page. Default: Disabled.
  • Progress bar color — Color for the progress bar. Default: Your primary color.
  • Enable back to top button — Show button to scroll back to top. Default: Enabled.

docs.title: Social Sharing
docs.text:
• Share buttons — Enable social sharing buttons. Default: Enabled.
  • Share title — Text above share buttons. Default: "Share this article".

Platforms included: - Facebook - Twitter (X) - Pinterest - Email - WhatsApp

docs.title: Article Structure
docs.text: The page displays: 1. Featured Image — Large hero image at top (if article has one) 2. Article Title — Main headline 3. Article Info — Author and date (if enabled) 4. Article Content — Full blog post body with formatting 5. Share Buttons — Social sharing options (if enabled) 6. Back to Top Button — Floating button (if enabled)

docs.title: Managing Articles
docs.text:
Article content is managed in your Shopify admin:

  1. Go to Online Store > Blog Posts
  2. Select your blog
  3. Click on an article to edit:
  4. Title — Article headline
  5. Content — Full article text (rich text editor)
  6. Excerpt — Short summary for article cards
  7. Featured Image — Main image (recommended: 1200x800px)
  8. Author — Writer name
  9. Tags — Topics for organization
  10. SEO — Meta description and URL
  11. Save changes

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Featured images: Always include high-quality featured images. They're displayed prominently and shared on social media.

  • Formatting: Use the rich text editor to:

  • Add headings for structure
  • Break text into short paragraphs
  • Include bullet points and lists
  • Insert images throughout longer articles

  • Add links to related products or articles

  • Content width: If you have long-form articles, consider using a narrower container width (700-800px) for easier reading.

  • Progress bar: Enable for longer articles (1000+ words) so readers can see how far they've read.

  • Author info: Display author names to build credibility and personal connection.

  • Share buttons: Make it easy for readers to share your content. Social sharing drives traffic.

  • Back to top: Helpful for long articles so readers can easily navigate back to the top.

  • Mobile readability: Test articles on mobile. Ensure images scale properly and text is readable.

docs.title: Content
docs.text:
• Compelling titles: Write clear, benefit-driven headlines that make people want to read.
  • Strong opening: Hook readers in the first paragraph.
  • Scannable format: Use headings, short paragraphs, bullet points, and images.
  • Value-focused: Provide useful information, not just promotional content.
  • Call-to-action: End with a clear next step (shop products, read related articles, leave a comment).

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
• Featured image: Use high-quality, relevant images (recommended: 1200x800px or 16:9 ratio).
  • In-content images: Break up text with relevant images every 300-500 words.
  • Alt text: Add descriptive alt text to all images for accessibility and SEO.
  • Consistent style: Use similar image styles across all articles for visual consistency.

docs.title: SEO
docs.text:
• Meta description: Write compelling descriptions (150-160 characters) in the article editor.
  • URL handle: Use clear, keyword-rich URLs (e.g., /blogs/news/summer-collection-guide).
  • Internal links: Link to related products, collections, or other articles.
  • Keywords: Include relevant keywords naturally in title, headings, and content.
  • Tags: Use consistent tags for topic organization and SEO.

docs.title: Engagement
docs.text:
• Enable comments: Allow customer interaction (if your blog supports comments).
  • Respond promptly: Reply to comments to build community.
  • Social promotion: Share articles on your social media channels.
  • Email newsletter: Feature new articles in email campaigns.

docs.title: Reading Progress Bar
docs.text:
The progress bar feature shows a thin colored line at the top of the page that fills as customers scroll through the article. It helps readers: - See how much content remains - Gauge time commitment - Feel progress toward completion

When to use: - Long-form content (1000+ words) - In-depth guides and tutorials - Story-driven articles

When to skip: - Short articles (under 500 words) - News briefs or announcements - Image-heavy posts

docs.title: Social Sharing Strategy
docs.text:
Social sharing buttons help amplify your content reach:

  • Placement: Sharing buttons appear at the end of articles after readers finish.
  • Multiple platforms: Offer several options to match reader preferences.
  • Pre-filled content: Sharing includes article title and URL automatically.
  • Featured image: When shared, your featured image appears on social platforms.

Optimize for sharing: - Use eye-catching featured images (they appear in social previews) - Write compelling titles (they become the share text) - Add meta descriptions (appear in link previews) - Test how shares look on different platforms

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about blog articles, visit: - Writing blog posts - Blog SEO - Adding images to posts - Blog best practices

docs.title: Blog Page Template
docs.text:
The Blog Page template displays a collection of blog posts with optional sidebar, search functionality, and tag filtering. This is the main page customers see when accessing your blog.

This is a template section that controls the layout and features of your blog listing page.

docs.title: Important Note
docs.text:
This template only appears on blog pages. You customize it by: 1. Going to your Theme Editor 2. Navigating to any blog page (or selecting "Blog" > "Default blog") 3. Adjusting the Blog pages section settings

Blog posts themselves are managed in Online Store > Blog Posts in your Shopify admin.

docs.title: Colors & Layout
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the background color for the blog header area. Default: Scheme 1.
  • Articles color scheme — Choose the color scheme specifically for article cards and sidebar. Default: Scheme 1.

Tip: Using different color schemes for the header and articles can create nice visual separation.

docs.title: Display Options
docs.text:
• Articles per page — How many blog posts to show before pagination. Range: 1-50 articles. Default: 24.

Note: More articles per page means fewer clicks, but longer page load times. 12-24 is usually optimal.

docs.title: Sidebar
docs.text:
• Show sidebar — Enable to display a sidebar with tags and search functionality. Default: Enabled.

Sidebar contents (when enabled): - Tag cloud for filtering posts by topic - Article search box

Layout: - With sidebar: Articles display in 3 columns (desktop), sidebar on left - Without sidebar: Articles display in wider grid across full width

docs.title: Blog Header
docs.text:
• Heading — Main title for your blog. Default: Uses your blog's name (e.g., "{{ blog.title }}").

  • Heading tag — HTML tag for SEO (H1-H6 or Span). Default: H1.

  • Tip: Use H1 for your blog title for proper SEO structure.

  • Heading size — Visual size of the heading:

  • Title 1 — Largest
  • Title 2 — Large
  • H1-H6 — Standard sizes

Default: H1.

  • Heading font weight — Text thickness. Range: 100 (thin) to 900 (bold). Default: 700 (bold).

  • Introduction — Optional introductory text explaining what your blog is about.

docs.title: Sidebar Settings (when enabled)
docs.text:
• Show blog tags — Enable to display tag cloud in sidebar. Default: Enabled.

  • Blog tags title — Heading for the tags section. Default: "Topics" or similar.

  • Show search box — Enable article search functionality in sidebar. Default: Enabled.

  • Search box title — Heading for the search section. Default: "Search Articles" or similar.

docs.title: Spacing
docs.text:
• Margin top — Space above the section. Options: Standard or None. Default: Standard.
  • Margin bottom — Space below the section. Options: Standard or None. Default: Standard.
  • Padding top — Inner spacing at the top. Options: Standard or None. Default: Standard.
  • Padding bottom — Inner spacing at the bottom. Options: Standard or None. Default: Standard.

docs.title: Creating and Managing Blogs
docs.text:
Blogs are managed in your Shopify admin:

  1. Go to Online Store > Blog Posts
  2. Click Manage blogs to create or edit blogs
  3. Click Add blog to create a new blog
  4. Name your blog (e.g., "News", "Guides", "Company Blog")
  5. Add SEO details
  6. Save

docs.title: Creating Blog Posts
docs.text:
To add articles to your blog:

  1. Go to Online Store > Blog Posts
  2. Select the blog you want to add to
  3. Click Add blog post
  4. Enter:
  5. Title — Post headline
  6. Content — Article body (use rich text editor)
  7. Excerpt — Short summary (appears in article cards)
  8. Featured image — Main image (recommended: 1200x800px)
  9. Author — Writer name
  10. Tags — Topics for organization and filtering
  11. SEO — Meta description and URL handle
  12. Set visibility (published, hidden, or scheduled)
  13. Save

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Tags help organize your blog posts and allow customers to filter by topic.

Adding tags to posts: 1. Edit a blog post in your Shopify admin 2. Scroll to the "Organization" section 3. Add tags (e.g., "tutorials", "news", "product updates") 4. Save

How tags work: - Tags appear as clickable badges in the sidebar - Customers can click a tag to see all posts with that tag - Tags in URLs show as: /blogs/blog-name/tagged/tag-name

Tag best practices: - Use consistent, lowercase tags - Create 5-10 main tags, not hundreds of unique tags - Think about topics customers would want to browse

docs.title: Search Functionality
docs.text:
The sidebar search box allows customers to search articles by keywords:

  • Searches article titles, content, and excerpts
  • Results show relevant posts ranked by relevance
  • Search is case-insensitive
  • Returns published posts only

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text: When you have more articles than the "per page" setting: - Pagination controls appear at the bottom - Customers can navigate between pages - URL changes to include page number - SEO-friendly pagination links

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Sidebar or no sidebar:
  • Use sidebar if you have many posts across multiple topics (helps with navigation)

  • Skip sidebar for cleaner look if you have fewer posts or prefer minimalism

  • Featured images: Always add high-quality featured images to blog posts. They're crucial for visual appeal in the grid layout.

  • Consistent image sizes: Use the same aspect ratio for all blog featured images (16:9 or 4:3 recommended) for a uniform grid.

  • Compelling excerpts: Write custom excerpts for each post. These appear in article cards and influence click-through rates.

  • Tags organization: Use tags strategically as navigation categories, not just keywords. Examples:

  • "How-to"
  • "Product News"
  • "Customer Stories"

  • "Industry Insights"

  • Regular publishing: Maintain an active blog with regular posts. Aim for at least one post per month minimum.

  • Mobile experience: The grid adjusts to 2 columns on mobile. Test to ensure article cards remain readable and images look good.

  • Blog introduction: Use the introduction text to set expectations about what customers will find in your blog.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Content strategy: Plan blog topics that:
  • Answer customer questions
  • Showcase product usage
  • Provide value beyond selling
  • Target relevant SEO keywords

  • Establish your expertise

  • Visual quality: Use professional, consistent imagery. Poor images hurt your brand.

  • Post structure: Format blog posts with:

  • Clear headings and subheadings
  • Short paragraphs (2-4 sentences)
  • Bullet points for lists
  • Images throughout longer posts

  • Call-to-action at the end

  • SEO optimization:

  • Write descriptive titles (50-60 characters)
  • Add meta descriptions (150-160 characters)
  • Use relevant keywords naturally
  • Add internal links to products or other posts

  • Optimize images with alt text

  • Engagement: Enable comments if you want customer interaction. Respond to comments promptly.

  • Promotion: Share blog posts on:

  • Social media
  • Email newsletters
  • Homepage (use Articles section)
  • Product pages (if relevant)

docs.title: Multiple Blogs
docs.text:
You can create multiple blogs for different purposes:

  • News blog — Company updates and announcements
  • How-to blog — Tutorials and guides
  • Customer stories — Testimonials and case studies
  • Industry blog — Trends and insights

Each blog gets its own URL and can be displayed separately on your site.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about blogging, visit: - Adding and managing blogs - Blog SEO best practices - Blog post tagging

docs.title: Cart Page Template
docs.text: The Cart Page template displays the shopping cart where customers review items, adjust quantities, and proceed to checkout. This is a crucial page in the purchase flow.

docs.title: Colors & Layout
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Background color for the cart page. Default: Scheme 1.
  • Card color scheme — Color scheme for individual cart item cards. Default: Scheme 2.
  • No margin bottom — Remove bottom spacing. Default: Enabled.

docs.title: Heading
docs.text:
• Heading — Cart page title. Default: "Shopping Cart".
  • Heading tag — HTML tag (H1-H6). Default: H1.
  • Heading size — Visual size (Title 1, Title 2, H1-H6). Default: H1.
  • Heading font weight — Text thickness (100-900). Default: 700.
  • Content — Optional description text below heading.

docs.title: Cart Items Display
docs.text:
• Item image size — Size of product thumbnails (pixels). Range: 50-200px. Default: 100px.
  • Item title size — Product name text size. Default: H5.
  • Item title font weight — Product name thickness (100-900). Default: 700.

docs.title: Empty Cart
docs.text:
• Empty cart heading — Title shown when cart is empty. Default: "Your cart is empty".
  • Empty cart heading size — Size of empty message. Default: H3.
  • Empty cart heading font weight — Thickness (100-900). Default: 700.
  • Empty cart content — Description when cart is empty.

docs.title: For Each Item:
docs.text:
• Product image (clickable to product page)
  • Product name and variant
  • Individual price
  • Quantity adjuster (+ / - buttons or trash icon if qty = 1)
  • Line total (price × quantity)
  • Expandable details (variants, options)

docs.title: Cart Summary (Sidebar):
docs.text:
• Subtotal
  • Estimated taxes
  • Shipping calculation
  • Total
  • Checkout button
  • Payment icons
  • Trust badges/USPs

docs.title: USP Block
docs.text: Add trust signals in the cart sidebar: * Icon — Font Awesome icon (e.g., fa-solid fa-lock). * Icon color — Choose icon color. * Text — USP message (e.g., "Secure Checkout"). * No margin bottom — Remove spacing below USP.

docs.title: App Block
docs.text: Integrate third-party apps (discount codes, upsells, etc.).

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Clear CTAs: Make the checkout button prominent and easy to find.
  • Trust signals: Add USPs like "Secure Checkout", "Free Shipping", "Easy Returns".
  • Empty cart: Provide clear next steps with "Continue Shopping" button.
  • Mobile: Test quantity adjusters work well on touchscreens.
  • Shipping calculator: Consider adding estimated shipping costs.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Keep the cart simple and focused on checkout
  • Show item images so customers can verify their selections
  • Make quantity adjustment intuitive
  • Display total costs clearly (subtotal, taxes, shipping, total)
  • Include trust badges to reduce checkout anxiety
  • Optimize for mobile—most cart abandonment happens on mobile

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text:
• Managing your cart page
  • Reducing cart abandonment

docs.title: Collection Page Template
docs.text:
The Collection Page displays groups of products organized together, allowing customers to browse and filter products by category, type, or any custom grouping you create.

This is a template section that controls the overall layout, filtering options, and display settings for all your collection pages.

docs.title: Important Note
docs.text: This is a template section that appears automatically on all collection pages. You customize it by: 1. Going to your Theme Editor 2. Navigating to any collection page (or selecting "Collections" > "Default collection") 3. Adjusting the settings in the "Collection pages" section

docs.title: Colors & Styling
docs.text:
• Color scheme — Choose the background color and text style for the collection page. Default: Scheme 1.
  • Filters color scheme — Choose a separate color scheme specifically for the filter sidebar/panel. This allows you to visually separate the filtering area from the main product grid. Default: Scheme 2.

docs.title: Heading
docs.text:
• Heading tag — Choose the HTML heading level for the collection title:
  • H1 — Main page heading (recommended for SEO)
  • H2 — Subheading level
  • Title 1 — Large display title
  • Title 2 — Medium display title

Default: H1.

  • Heading size — Control the visual size of the collection title:
  • Title 1 — Largest size
  • Title 2 — Medium size
  • H1 — Standard heading size
  • H2 — Smaller heading size

Default: Title 1.

  • Font weight — Set the thickness of the heading text. Range: 100 (thin) to 900 (bold). Default: 400 (normal).

docs.title: Product Grid Layout
docs.text:
• Products per row (desktop) — Choose how many products display side-by-side on desktop:
  • 3 columns — Fewer products, larger images
  • 4 columns — Balanced layout (recommended)
  • 5 columns — More products, smaller images

Default: 4 columns.

  • Products per row (mobile) — Choose the mobile layout:
  • 1 column — One product per row, largest view
  • 2 columns — Two products side-by-side

Default: 2 columns.

  • Products per page — Set how many products load on each page before pagination. Range: 12-48 products. Default: 24.

docs.title: Margins & Padding
docs.text:
Control the outer spacing (margin) and inner spacing (padding) for the collection page:

  • Margin top — Space above the collection section. Range: 0-30. Default: 0.
  • Margin bottom — Space below the collection section. Range: 0-30. Default: 0.
  • Padding top — Inner spacing at the top. Range: 0-30. Default: 0.
  • Padding bottom — Inner spacing at the bottom. Range: 0-30. Default: 0.

docs.title: Product Filtering & Sorting
docs.text: Your collection pages automatically include filtering and sorting functionality:

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Filters help customers narrow down products by attributes like: - Price range - Product type - Color, size, or other variants - Product tags - Availability (in stock)

Setting up filters: Filters are configured in your Shopify admin under Online Store > Navigation > Filters. The theme automatically displays any filters you've enabled for your collections.

docs.title: Sorting
docs.text:
Customers can sort products by: - Featured (your custom order) - Best selling - Alphabetically (A-Z or Z-A) - Price (low to high or high to low) - Date (newest or oldest)

The sort dropdown appears automatically on collection pages.

docs.title: Managing Collections
docs.text:
Collections themselves are created and managed in your Shopify admin:

  1. Go to Products > Collections
  2. Click "Create collection"
  3. Add products manually or use automated conditions
  4. Set a collection image and description
  5. Save your changes

The collection page template will automatically display your collections with the layout and styling you've configured.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Grid layout: Choose your grid layout based on your product imagery. If you have detailed product photos, use fewer columns (3) for larger images. If products are more uniform, 4-5 columns can work well.

  • Mobile-first: Most customers shop on mobile, so always preview your collections on a phone. The 2-column mobile layout usually works best.

  • Filter organization: Organize your filters logically (e.g., Type, then Size, then Color) to help customers find products quickly.

  • Products per page: Balance page load time with browsing convenience. 24-48 products per page is usually ideal.

  • Collection descriptions: Add helpful descriptions to your collections (in the Shopify admin) to improve SEO and help customers understand what they're browsing.

  • Color schemes: Using a different color scheme for filters can help them stand out, making it clear where customers can refine their search.

  • Featured products: Set your best or seasonal products as "featured" in the collection, and customers can sort to see them first.

  • Collection images: Add attractive collection images in your Shopify admin—they often display at the top of collection pages as banners.

docs.title: Collection Types
docs.text:
There are two types of collections:

  • Manual collections — You choose exactly which products to include
  • Automated collections — Products are added automatically based on conditions (like product type, price, tag, etc.)

Both types display using the same template settings.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about managing collections, visit: - Creating collections - Product filters - Organizing products

docs.title: List Collections Page Template
docs.text: The List Collections page displays all your store's collections in a grid, giving customers an overview of all product categories. This page typically appears at /collections.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• No margin bottom — Remove bottom spacing below the section. Default: Enabled.
  • Color scheme — Background color and text style. Default: Scheme 1.
  • Pagination color scheme — Color scheme for pagination controls. Default: Scheme 1.

docs.title: Display
docs.text: • Collections per page — How many collections to show before pagination. Range: 1-50. Default: 24.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The page automatically displays: - All published collections in your store - Collection featured images - Collection titles - Links to each collection page

Collections appear in a responsive grid: - Desktop: 4 columns (col-lg-3) - Tablet: 3 columns (col-sm-4) - Mobile: 2 columns (col-6)

docs.title: Collection Cards
docs.text:
Each collection is displayed as a card showing: - Collection featured image - Collection title - Number of products (optional, based on theme settings) - Link to collection page

Card appearance is controlled by your theme's global collection card settings (Theme Settings > Collection Cards).

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Featured images: Add attractive featured images to all collections for visual appeal.
  • Naming: Use clear, descriptive collection names that tell customers what they'll find.
  • Organization: Organize collections logically (by category, season, style, etc.).
  • Homepage link: Add a prominent link to this page from your homepage or main navigation.
  • Collections per page: 24 collections is usually sufficient. Adjust if you have many collections.

docs.title: Managing Collections
docs.text:
Collections are managed in your Shopify admin:

  1. Go to Products > Collections
  2. Create, edit, or delete collections
  3. Add featured images
  4. Write descriptions
  5. Set collection rules (manual or automated)

Changes automatically appear on the List Collections page.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• High-quality images: Use consistent, professional images for all collections (recommended: 800x800px minimum).
  • Strategic organization: Create collections that match how customers think about your products.
  • Collection descriptions: Add descriptions for SEO—they help search engines understand your collections.
  • Seasonal collections: Update regularly with seasonal or promotional collections to keep content fresh.
  • Navigation: Include a "Shop All" or "All Collections" link in your main menu.

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text:
• Main categories: "Men's", "Women's", "Kids"
  • Product types: "Shoes", "Tops", "Accessories"
  • Occasions: "Summer", "Workwear", "Formal"
  • Features: "New Arrivals", "Sale", "Best Sellers"
  • Brands: Collections organized by brand or manufacturer

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information, visit: - Creating collections - Collection images - Organizing products

docs.title: Product Page Template
docs.text:
The Product Page is where customers view detailed information about a specific product, see images, read descriptions, select variants, and add items to their cart.

This is a template section that controls the overall layout and spacing of your product pages. The actual product content (images, description, specifications, etc.) is managed through additional sections that you can add and arrange on product pages.

docs.title: Important Note
docs.text: This is a template section that appears automatically on all product pages. You customize it by: 1. Going to your Theme Editor 2. Navigating to any product page 3. Adjusting the settings in the "Product pages" section

docs.title: Colors & Styling
docs.text: • Color scheme — Choose the background color and text style for the entire product page. Default: Scheme 1.

docs.title: Spacing
docs.text: • Space between sections — Control the vertical spacing between different sections on your product pages (like between the main product area, description, recommendations, etc.). Range: 0-30px. Default: 20px.

docs.title: Margins & Padding
docs.text:
Control the outer spacing (margin) and inner spacing (padding) for the product page:

  • Margin top — Space above the product section. Range: 0-30. Default: 0.
  • Margin bottom — Space below the product section. Range: 0-30. Default: 0.
  • Padding top — Inner spacing at the top. Range: 0-30. Default: 0.
  • Padding bottom — Inner spacing at the bottom. Range: 0-30. Default: 0.

docs.title: Building Your Product Page
docs.text:
The product page template works together with several product-specific sections:

  1. Main Product Section — Shows product images, title, price, variant selectors, and Add to Cart button
  2. Product Description — Displays the full product description
  3. Product Specifications — Shows technical details and features in a structured format
  4. Product Recommendations — Suggests related products to customers

You can add, remove, and rearrange these sections in the Theme Editor to create the perfect product page layout for your store.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Consistent spacing: Use the "Space between sections" setting to create visual separation between different areas of your product page, making it easier to scan.

  • Clean layout: Avoid adding too many sections to product pages. Focus on what customers need to make a purchase decision.

  • Mobile optimization: Always preview your product pages on mobile devices. Most shoppers browse on phones, so ensure images are clear and buttons are easy to tap.

  • Color schemes: Use color schemes that provide good contrast for readability. Product pages need to be easy to read quickly.

  • Test the flow: Walk through the entire buying process as a customer would—viewing the product, selecting options, and adding to cart.

  • Image quality: While not controlled by this template, ensure your product images are high-quality and show products from multiple angles.

docs.title: Customizing Product Information
docs.text:
Product details (title, price, description, images, etc.) are managed in your Shopify admin:

  1. Go to Products in your Shopify admin
  2. Click on the product you want to edit
  3. Update the information as needed
  4. Save your changes

The template automatically displays this information in the appropriate sections.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about managing products, visit: - Adding and updating products - Product variants

docs.title: Search Results Page Template
docs.text: The Search Results page displays products, articles, and pages that match a customer's search query. This template controls how search results are organized and displayed, making it easy for customers to find what they're looking for.

docs.title: Important Note
docs.text: This template only appears on search results pages (/search). You customize it by: 1. Going to your Theme Editor 2. In the page selector, choose Search or navigate to /search?q=test in your browser 3. Adjusting the Search section settings

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• No margin bottom — Enable to remove bottom spacing below this section. Default: Enabled.

  • Color scheme — Choose the background color for the search info card. Default: Scheme 2.

docs.title: Heading
docs.text:
• Heading tag — HTML tag for the search term heading (H1-H6 or Span). Default: H1.

  • Heading size — Visual size of the search term:

  • Title 1 — Largest
  • Title 2 — Large
  • H1-H6 — Standard sizes

Default: H1.

  • Heading font weight — Text thickness. Range: 100-900. Default: 700 (bold).

docs.title: Display Settings
docs.text:
• Results per page — How many results to show before pagination. Range: 1-50. Default: 24.

  • Products per row (desktop) — Number of product columns on desktop. Options: col-md-3 (4 columns), col-md-4 (3 columns), col-md-6 (2 columns). Default: col-md-4 (3 columns).

docs.title: What the Search Page Shows
docs.text: The search results page displays three types of content that match the search query:

docs.title: Products
docs.text:
• Displayed as product cards with images, titles, and prices
  • Use your theme's standard product card styling
  • Sortable using the dropdown menu

docs.title: Articles (Blog Posts)
docs.text:
• Shown as article cards with featured images and titles
  • Link directly to the full blog post
  • Help drive traffic to your content

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
• Displayed as simple cards with page titles
  • Link to the full page
  • Useful for finding policy pages, about pages, etc.

All results appear in a mixed grid, with products typically displayed most prominently.

docs.title: Sort Options
docs.text:
Customers can sort search results by: - Relevance (default—best matches first) - Price (low to high or high to low) - Newest first - Best selling - Alphabetically (A-Z or Z-A)

The sort dropdown appears in the top-right of the search info card.

docs.title: Results Count
docs.text: The page automatically displays how many total results were found for the search term.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text: If there are more results than fit on one page, pagination controls appear at the bottom, allowing customers to browse through all results.

docs.title: How Search Works
docs.text:
Shopify's built-in search indexes: - Product titles - Product descriptions - Product variants and SKUs - Product tags - Product types - Product vendors - Collection titles - Page titles and content - Blog post titles and content

Search is: - Case-insensitive — "camera" and "Camera" return the same results - Partial matching — Searching "run" finds "running", "runner", etc. - Multi-word — Searching "blue shirt" finds products with both words

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Empty state: If no results are found, Shopify displays a "No results" message. Consider adding suggested collections or products to this page.

  • Search bar placement: Make sure your search bar is easily accessible in your header (configured in Theme Settings > Header).

  • Product titles matter: Well-written product titles with relevant keywords improve search results.

  • Tag strategy: Use consistent, descriptive tags—they're searchable and help customers find products.

  • Page content: Optimize your page content (About, FAQ, etc.) with keywords customers might search for.

  • Blog integration: Having a blog increases searchable content on your site, improving the usefulness of search.

docs.title: Optimize Product Data
docs.text: Make products easier to find by: - Writing clear, descriptive product titles - Including relevant keywords in descriptions - Adding comprehensive tags - Filling in product type and vendor fields - Including variant names customers might search for

docs.title: Synonym Groups
docs.text:
In Shopify, you can create synonym groups to handle common variations: - "tshirt" = "t-shirt" = "t shirt" - "sneaker" = "trainer" = "athletic shoe"

Set these up in Settings > Store > Search in your Shopify admin.

docs.title: Stop Words
docs.text: Shopify automatically ignores common words like "the", "and", "or" to improve search relevance.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Results per page: 24 results balances discoverability with page load time. Adjust based on your catalog size.

  • Mixed content types: Showing products, articles, and pages in the same results helps customers find whatever they're looking for.

  • Clear headings: The search term is displayed as the heading (e.g., "red dress") so customers know what they searched for.

  • Sort accessibility: Make sure the sort dropdown is visible and easy to use, especially on mobile devices.

  • Mobile layout: Products automatically stack into fewer columns on mobile (typically 2 columns). Test to ensure cards remain readable.

  • No results handling: If customers frequently search for items you don't have, consider:

  • Adding those products to your catalog
  • Creating content around those topics
  • Redirecting common "no result" searches to relevant collections

docs.title: Search Analytics
docs.text:
Monitor search behavior in your Shopify analytics:

  1. Go to Analytics > Reports in your Shopify admin
  2. Look for Online store search reports
  3. See:
  4. Top search terms
  5. Searches with no results
  6. Search-to-purchase conversion

Use this data to: - Identify popular products to promote - Find gaps in your product catalog - Improve product titles and descriptions - Create content around popular searches

docs.title: Search Suggestions
docs.text: Enable search suggestions in your header (Theme Settings > Header) to show popular searches or collections as customers type.

docs.title: Filters on Search Results
docs.text: While basic search shows all matching results, customers can use your collection filters after clicking through to specific categories.

docs.title: Third-Party Search Apps
docs.text: For advanced search features, consider Shopify apps that offer: - Autocomplete with thumbnails - Typo tolerance - Advanced filtering - Search analytics - Merchandising controls

docs.title: Common Search Issues
docs.text:
Products not appearing in search: - Ensure products are published and available - Check product titles and descriptions contain relevant keywords - Verify products aren't hidden or password-protected

Irrelevant results: - Remove unnecessary tags that create false matches - Refine product descriptions to focus on relevant terms - Use more specific product titles

Too many results: - Encourage customers to use more specific search terms - Implement synonym groups to consolidate variants - Ensure product categorization is clear

docs.title: Technical Notes
docs.text:
• Search results are generated by Shopify's search engine—you can't customize the search algorithm itself.

  • The search parameter in URLs is ?q=search-term.

  • Search is available in all languages if you have a multi-language store.

  • Search respects your inventory settings—out-of-stock products appear based on your visibility preferences.

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about search, visit: - Understanding Shopify search - Improving search results - Search best practices

docs.title: Product Description Section
docs.text:
The Product Description section displays the detailed product description on your product pages. It shows the full description you've entered in your Shopify admin, along with optional title, icons, and app integrations.

This section is specifically designed for product pages and helps customers understand what they're buying.

docs.title: Important Note
docs.text:
This section only appears on product pages. You customize it by: 1. Going to your Theme Editor 2. Navigating to any product page (or selecting "Products" > "Default product") 3. Finding the Product Description section 4. Adjusting settings or adding blocks

The actual product description content is managed in your Shopify admin under Products.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• No margin bottom — Enable to remove the bottom spacing below this section (useful if you're stacking multiple product sections closely together). Default: Enabled.

  • Color scheme — Choose the background color and text style. Default: Scheme 1.

docs.title: Text Settings
docs.text:
• Text alignment — Align the description text:
  • Left — Left-aligned (standard for readability)
  • Center — Centered
  • Right — Right-aligned

Default: Left.

docs.title: Title Block
docs.text:
Add an optional title above the product description. Limit: 1 title block.

Settings:

  • Heading — The title text to display. Default: "Information & Details".

  • Heading tag — Choose the HTML tag for SEO:

  • H1-H6 — Standard heading tags
  • Span — Not a heading (for styling only)

Default: H2.

Tip: Choose the tag based on your SEO strategy. This doesn't affect the visual size.

  • Heading size — Control the visual size of the title:
  • Title 1 — Largest
  • Title 2 — Large
  • H1-H6 — Standard sizes

Default: H2.

  • Heading font weight — Text thickness. Range: 100 (thin) to 900 (bold). Default: 700 (bold).

docs.title: Icon Block
docs.text:
Add icon blocks to highlight key product features or benefits below the description. These appear in a centered grid below your description text.

Settings for each Icon:

  • Icon — Font Awesome icon code (e.g., fa-solid fa-truck-fast). Default: "fa-solid fa-check".

  • Find icons at fontawesome.com

  • Heading — Title for this feature. Example: "Fast Shipping".

  • Text — Description text explaining the feature.

Icons automatically display in a responsive grid (up to 4 columns on desktop, stacking on mobile).

docs.title: App Block
docs.text: Integrate third-party Shopify apps into your product description area. Apps that support product page blocks will appear as options when you add an App block.

docs.title: Managing Product Descriptions
docs.text:
The actual product description content is managed in your Shopify admin:

  1. Go to Products in your Shopify admin
  2. Select the product you want to edit
  3. Scroll to the Description field
  4. Enter your product description using the rich text editor
  5. Save your changes

The theme automatically displays this description in the Product Description section.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Clear structure: Use the title block to add a heading like "Product Details" or "About This Product" to visually separate the description from other page elements.

  • Formatting: Format your product descriptions in the Shopify admin with:

  • Bullet points for features
  • Bold text for emphasis

  • Short paragraphs for readability

  • Icon features: Use icon blocks to highlight important selling points:

  • Shipping and delivery
  • Warranty or guarantees
  • Quality certifications
  • Return policy

  • Customer support

  • Icon selection: Choose icons that clearly represent each feature. Keep icons consistent in style (all solid or all outlined).

  • Don't duplicate: The description automatically pulls from your product data—you don't need to retype it in the theme settings.

  • Mobile readability: Long paragraphs are hard to read on mobile. Break content into shorter chunks with headings and lists.

  • App integrations: Many review apps, size charts, and product enhancement apps can be added via the App block.

  • SEO considerations: Use the heading tag setting strategically. If your product title is H1, make the description title H2 for proper heading hierarchy.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Be descriptive: Help customers make informed decisions by explaining:
  • What the product is and what it does
  • Key features and specifications
  • Materials and quality
  • Sizing or compatibility information

  • Care instructions

  • Tell a story: Beyond just listing features, explain how the product benefits the customer and solves their problem.

  • Use keywords naturally: Include relevant search terms customers might use, but write for humans first.

  • Keep it scannable: Use short paragraphs, bullet points, and subheadings to make information easy to find.

  • Update regularly: Refresh descriptions as you learn what questions customers ask or what features they care about most.

docs.title: Common Icon Block Examples
docs.text:
• Shipping: fa-solid fa-truck + "Free Shipping Over $50"
  • Returns: fa-solid fa-rotate-left + "30-Day Easy Returns"
  • Warranty: fa-solid fa-shield-halved + "1-Year Warranty Included"
  • Quality: fa-solid fa-certificate + "Premium Quality Materials"
  • Support: fa-solid fa-headset + "24/7 Customer Support"
  • Secure: fa-solid fa-lock + "Secure Checkout"

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about product descriptions, visit: - Adding product details - Product description best practices

docs.title: Product Recommendations Section
docs.text:
The Product Recommendations section automatically displays products related to the current product being viewed. Shopify uses AI to suggest products based on purchase patterns, product attributes, and customer behavior.

This section helps increase average order value by showing customers additional items they might be interested in.

docs.title: Important Note
docs.text:
This section only appears on product pages. Recommendations are automatically generated by Shopify based on: - Products frequently bought together - Products with similar attributes - Complementary products from the same collection - Your specified recommendation intent

You customize it by: 1. Going to your Theme Editor 2. Navigating to any product page (or selecting "Products" > "Default product") 3. Finding the Product Recommendations section 4. Adjusting display settings

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• No margin bottom — Enable to remove bottom spacing below this section. Default: Enabled.

  • Color scheme — Choose the background color and text style. Default: Scheme 2.

  • Section type — Control the section width:

  • Edge to Edge — Content stretches full width
  • Box — Content contained within standard page width

Default: Box.

  • Section height — Background height behavior:
  • Fixed height — Background has a set height
  • Grow with content — Background adjusts to content

Default: Grow with content.

docs.title: Recommendation Settings
docs.text:
• Recommendation intent — Choose the type of recommendations:
  • Related — Products similar to the current product (most common)
  • Complementary — Products that complement or enhance the current product

Default: Related.

Example: If viewing a camera, "Related" might show other cameras, while "Complementary" might show lenses, memory cards, or camera bags.

docs.title: Display Settings
docs.text:
• Slides per view — Number of recommended products to show at once on desktop. Range: 2-6 products. Default: 4.

  • Carousel overflow — Enable to show a peek of the next product, encouraging scrolling. Default: Disabled.

  • Slider pagination — Show dot indicators below the carousel for navigation. Default: Enabled.

  • Alternate offset — Stagger every other product slightly lower for visual interest. Default: Disabled.

docs.title: Content
docs.text:
• Heading — Section title displayed above recommendations. Default: "You may also like" (or similar).

  • Heading tag — HTML tag for SEO (H1-H6 or Span). Default: H2.

  • Heading size — Visual size of the heading (Title 1, Title 2, or H1-H6). Default: H2.

  • Heading font weight — Text thickness. Range: 100-900. Default: 700 (bold).

  • Content — Optional description text below the heading.

  • Alignment — Position content:

  • Left — Left-aligned
  • Center — Centered
  • Right — Right-aligned

Default: Center.

docs.title: Button Block
docs.text:
Add call-to-action buttons above the recommendations (e.g., "View All Products" or "Shop Collection").

Settings:

  • Button label — Text displayed on the button.

  • Link — URL where the button leads (collection page, shop page, etc.).

  • Button style secondary — Enable for an outlined button style instead of solid. Default: Disabled (solid button).

You can add multiple button blocks if needed.

docs.title: How Recommendations Work
docs.text:
Shopify automatically generates product recommendations using machine learning. The system analyzes:

  • Customer behavior — What products are viewed or purchased together
  • Product attributes — Similar categories, tags, or product types
  • Collection membership — Products from related collections
  • Inventory availability — Only recommends products in stock (unless sold out items are enabled)

Important: Recommendations improve over time as your store gathers more sales data. New stores may see less accurate recommendations initially.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Heading copy: Choose headings that encourage exploration:
  • "You May Also Like"
  • "Customers Also Viewed"
  • "Complete the Look"
  • "Perfect Pairs"

  • "Recommended For You"

  • Intent setting:

  • Use Related for cross-selling similar products

  • Use Complementary for upselling additional items

  • Placement: This section typically works best:

  • Below the product description
  • After product specifications

  • Near the bottom of the product page

  • Styling: Use a contrasting color scheme (like Scheme 2) to make recommendations stand out from the main product area.

  • Multiple sections: You can add up to 2 Product Recommendations sections to the same product page with different intents (one for Related, one for Complementary).

  • No recommendations: If Shopify can't generate recommendations (new products, insufficient data), the section won't display anything—it won't show an empty state.

  • Test different intents: Try both Related and Complementary to see which generates better results for your products.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Strategic placement: Place recommendations where customers naturally look after reading about the product—usually lower on the page.

  • Clear headings: Use headings that create curiosity without being overly salesy.

  • Button options: Add buttons to direct customers to broader collection pages if they want more options.

  • Monitor performance: Check your analytics to see if recommendation sections lead to additional sales.

  • Product data quality: Ensure your products have:

  • Accurate product types
  • Relevant tags
  • Proper collection assignments

This helps Shopify generate better recommendations.

  • Inventory awareness: Shopify automatically excludes out-of-stock items from recommendations (based on your settings), keeping suggestions relevant.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Not seeing recommendations?

  • New products may not have enough data yet—recommendations improve over time
  • Products without similar items in your catalog won't generate recommendations
  • Check that you have sufficient product inventory and variety
  • Ensure products have tags, types, and collections properly configured

Recommendations not relevant?

  • Verify product categorization (types, tags, collections)
  • Try switching between Related and Complementary intents
  • Give the system time—recommendation quality improves as you get more sales data

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: For more information about product recommendations, visit: - Shopify product recommendations - Cross-selling and upselling strategies

docs.title: Product Specifications Section
docs.text:
The Product Specifications section displays technical details, features, and specifications for your products in a clean, organized table format. It's perfect for showing product dimensions, materials, compatibility, technical specs, and other structured information.

This section helps customers find specific product details quickly and makes informed purchase decisions.

docs.title: Important Note
docs.text: This section only appears on product pages. You customize it by: 1. Going to your Theme Editor 2. Navigating to any product page (or selecting "Products" > "Default product") 3. Finding the Product Specifications section 4. Adding specification rows with labels and values

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• No margin bottom — Enable to remove bottom spacing below this section. Default: Enabled.

  • Color scheme — Choose the background color and text style. Default: Scheme 1.

docs.title: Text Settings
docs.text:
• Text alignment — Align the section content:
  • Left — Left-aligned (recommended for specifications)
  • Center — Centered
  • Right — Right-aligned

Default: Left.

docs.title: Section Layout
docs.text:
The section displays: - Left side: Product's featured image (4 columns on desktop) - Right side: Specifications table in a card (8 columns on desktop)

On mobile, these stack vertically with the image on top.

docs.title: Title Block
docs.text:
Add an optional title above the specifications table. Limit: 1 title block.

Settings:

  • Heading — The title text to display. Default: "Specifications".

  • Heading tag — Choose the HTML tag for SEO:

  • H1-H6 — Standard heading tags
  • Span — Not a heading (for styling only)

Default: H2.

  • Heading size — Control the visual size:
  • Title 1 — Largest
  • Title 2 — Large
  • H1-H6 — Standard sizes

Default: H2.

  • Heading font weight — Text thickness. Range: 100 (thin) to 900 (bold). Default: 700 (bold).

docs.title: Row Block
docs.text:
Add specification rows to create your table. Each row has a label and a value.

Settings for each Row:

  • Label — The specification name (appears in bold on the left). Examples:
  • "Dimensions"
  • "Weight"
  • "Material"
  • "Color"

  • "Warranty"

  • Value — The specification detail (appears on the right). Examples:

  • "10 x 5 x 3 inches"
  • "2.5 lbs"
  • "Stainless steel"
  • "Matte black"
  • "2 years limited"

Add as many row blocks as you need to list all specifications.

docs.title: HTML Block
docs.text:
Add custom HTML content to the specifications area for more complex formatting needs.

Settings:

  • Content — Enter your custom HTML code.

This block is useful for advanced users who want to add custom layouts, embedded content, or special formatting that goes beyond simple specifications.

docs.title: Rich Text Block
docs.text:
Add formatted text content using Shopify's rich text editor.

Settings:

  • Content — Enter formatted text with bold, italic, lists, links, etc.

Use this for adding paragraphs of context, notes, or disclaimers related to the specifications.

docs.title: App Block
docs.text: Integrate third-party Shopify apps into your specifications area. Apps that support product page blocks will appear as options.

docs.title: Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Organization: Group related specifications together:
  • Physical attributes (dimensions, weight, color)
  • Technical specs (power, capacity, compatibility)
  • Materials and construction
  • Care and maintenance

  • Warranty and compliance

  • Consistent formatting: Keep labels and values formatted consistently:

  • Use the same units of measurement throughout
  • Capitalize labels consistently

  • Be precise with values

  • Common specifications to include:

  • Dimensions: Length x Width x Height (with units)
  • Weight: Product weight (shipping weight separate if needed)
  • Materials: What the product is made from
  • Color options: Available colors
  • SKU/Model number: For reference
  • Manufacturer: Brand name
  • Country of origin: Where it's made
  • Warranty: Coverage details

  • Certifications: Safety or quality certifications

  • Image selection: The section uses the product's featured image. Ensure your featured image clearly shows the product.

  • Mobile layout: The two-column layout (image + specs) stacks on mobile. Keep specification values concise so they're easy to read on small screens.

  • Title choice: Use titles like:

  • "Specifications"
  • "Technical Details"
  • "Product Information"

  • "Features & Specs"

  • Don't duplicate description: Keep specifications separate from your product description. Use specifications for factual data, and the description for benefits and storytelling.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Be specific: Provide exact measurements and details. Vague specifications don't help customers.

  • Use standard units: Stick to common measurement systems your customers understand (inches or cm, pounds or kg).

  • Include what matters: Focus on specifications customers need to know before buying. Not every detail needs to be listed.

  • Update regularly: Keep specifications current, especially if product materials or features change.

  • Test accuracy: Verify that all specifications are correct. Wrong dimensions or weights can lead to returns and dissatisfied customers.

  • Scannable format: The table format makes specifications easy to scan quickly—keep each row to a single line when possible.

  • Care instructions: Include care, maintenance, or assembly requirements if relevant.

  • Compliance information: Add required safety certifications, age recommendations, or regulatory information.
